[1. PURPOSE]
Vertical education app advertisement poster, app-install focused promo design for online classes and learning subscriptions. Rich commercial layout that feels like a real edtech subway poster and app launch campaign, combining a polished instructor portrait, dynamic learning-dashboard UI cards, discount messaging, QR download area, ratings, and short Korean promo copy.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Canvas: A4 vertical poster composition with a strong top-to-bottom reading flow, hero section occupying about 45% of the frame, text blocks stacked in clear modules, and a realistic print-ad finish for {비율}.
- Main subject placement: {hero} centered in the upper-middle hero area, with supporting {인플루언서·강사 컷} integrated as a secondary trust element on one side, overlapping the app UI cards like a real campaign composite.
- Background treatment: bright white base with blue accents, soft yellow highlight bars, pale grid-paper texture, faint notebook lines, small subject icons, translucent app-card layers, realistic paper grain, and soft studio shadows.
- Text spacing: headline at the top in a bold campaign block, CTA anchored near the lower third, QR/download strip at the bottom, rating and course-benefit chips arranged along an invisible 12-column grid.
- Use {앱·강의} as the primary product label, {헤드라인} as the main message, {CTA·할인} as the conversion block, {컬러 팔레트} as the palette reference, {비율} as the overall format constraint.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Top header zone: set {헤드라인} in large bold Korean typography, centered or slightly left-aligned, with a compact subtitle line underneath: 매일 15분, 새 스킬 1개. Add a small campaign label pill reading 2026 봄학기 런칭 특가.
- Hero zone: place {hero} as the main visual anchor, combining a lecture video mockup, progress graph, lesson checklist, streak calendar, quiz score tile, and student dashboard cards. Include small readable UI labels such as 오늘의 강의, 진도율 82%, 실전 퀴즈, 학습 리포트, 추천 강좌.
- Trust zone: add {인플루언서·강사 컷} as a realistic instructor portrait pair or a single confident mentor shot with microphone, tablet pen, laptop, sticky notes, and a warm testimonial banner. Include a model-name credit in small type: 강사 모델 김하린 · 데이터 분석 멘토.
- Product label zone: insert {앱·강의} as a concise app/course identifier near the hero or above the CTA, styled like a small category pill or app name tag. Add supporting benefit chips: 전과목 무제한, 초보자 맞춤, 수료 리포트 제공.
- Conversion zone: present {CTA·할인} in a bold button-like block at the lower section, visually separated with a strong color fill and high-contrast text. Include the exact offer line 첫 달 50% 할인, a coupon code badge NEW15, and a small deadline label 5월 31일까지.
- Bottom install strip: include a realistic QR code area, app-store style download badges, star rating 4.8, 리뷰 12,430개, small contact line help@learnnow.kr, and fine-print subscription note in Korean.
- Supporting graphic system: use progress bars, lesson cards, sticky memo tabs, pencil marks, soft geometric shapes, small emoji-like icons such as ✅ and ⚡, and layered UI widgets to reinforce the learning-app theme while keeping the poster clearly readable.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: Pretendard ExtraBold for the headline, Pretendard SemiBold for supporting lines, Noto Sans KR Medium for CTA details; headline size equivalent to 72–96px, body/supporting text 28–36px, microcopy 14–20px where appropriate.
- Color palette: use {컬러 팔레트} concretely as #2F6BFF blue, #FFD84D yellow, #FFFFFF white, #1F2937 charcoal; allow small light-gray UI neutrals like #E8EEF7, gentle sky-blue tints, and warm cream highlights.
- Border/shadow: rounded cards with 20–28px radius, soft drop shadow 0px 10px 24px rgba(31,41,55,0.12), thin 1px separators in pale blue, layered paper-like shadows, subtle glossy screen reflections on app mockups.
- Print realism: add tiny registration marks, a small poster code EDU-APP-0526 near the bottom edge, believable fine print, and a clean QR/download area that looks like an actual advertisement ready for print.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: clean commercial portrait + UI composite look, as if shot on an 85mm f/1.8 for the instructor cut and a top-down 35mm editorial setup for the app mockup cards.
- Lighting: soft studio key light from upper-left at 45°, gentle fill from front-right, slight edge light on the instructor cut, evenly exposed white background, realistic shadows under floating cards and hands.
- Color grade: crisp education-tech palette with bright blue and warm yellow accents, neutral whites, charcoal text, low saturation in skin tones, polished but not glossy.
- Material detail: include realistic laptop aluminum texture, tablet glass reflections, paper note texture, fabric detail in the instructor clothing, and tiny UI highlights to make the ad feel photographed and designed rather than flat.

[6. MOOD]
Modern edtech startup campaign — polished App Store / landing-page launch ad energy with the clarity of a Notion x Duolingo style commercial layout, upgraded with real print-poster density, friendly learning motivation, and a credible Korean subscription-service feel.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: the rendered image must correctly include these exact Korean strings: 매일 15분, 새 스킬 1개., 첫 달 50% 할인, 전과목 무제한.
- Additional Korean microcopy should be short and readable, including realistic ad details such as 2026 봄학기 런칭 특가, 오늘의 강의, 진도율 82%, 학습 리포트, NEW15, 5월 31일까지.
- Layout invariant: maintain a vertical A4 ad structure with clear hierarchy; hero + instructor cut + CTA + QR/download strip must all remain legible and separated.
- Do not distort the app/course label; {앱·강의} should read as a concise education product name.
- Keep all Korean typography clean, crisp, and fully readable with no broken characters.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters

[INPUT]

- output_size: 1024x1536

[1. PURPOSE]
Vertical fintech and banking app advertisement for social media and app-install promotion.
Realistic premium Korean fintech campaign poster presenting a mobile banking app, persuasive product proof points, security-oriented trust cues, promotion details, app-store download cues, and a conversion-focused CTA.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Full-page A4 vertical layout in 1024x1536 with a strong central phone mockup occupying about 42% of the frame height.
- Top headline area takes 18% of the canvas, centered and bold, supported by a small campaign label such as “2026 모바일 금융 캠페인” and “VOL.05 APP LAUNCH”.
- Mid section holds the hero phone mockup and fingertip tap interaction, with supporting UI cards, floating transaction chips, security notice bubbles, and small payment/transfer icons arranged around it.
- Lower section stacks 3 trust cards and a CTA / incentive block, plus a QR download area, app store badge area, promo period line, tiny legal disclaimer, and contact/support micro text.
- Use {앱·서비스}, {헤드라인}, {hero}, {포인트 박스}, {CTA·인센티브}, {컬러 팔레트}, {비율} placeholders.
- Background should feel like a polished real fintech ad set: soft gradient brand surface, faint abstract city-grid banking pattern, subtle glass reflections, lightweight paper/card texture, and realistic depth behind the phone while preserving clear readability.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Header area (top 18%): set {헤드라인} in large bold Korean sans-serif, centered, with strong visual hierarchy and tight line spacing. Add a small upper eyebrow label in Korean: “오늘의 금융 루틴” and a date label “2026.05.01–05.31”.
2. Service cue: integrate {앱·서비스} directly under the headline as a secondary descriptor, paired with small microcopy such as “송금 · 소비관리 · 자산조회 한 번에”.
3. Hero area (middle 42%): place {hero} as the main focal point, with the phone mockup front-facing and slightly angled for depth; show app screens with transfer complete, balance, and chart states clearly visible. Add realistic UI labels inside the phone such as “이체 완료”, “잔액 2,480,000원”, “이번 달 소비 분석”, and a small chart tooltip “+12.4%”.
4. Floating fintech detail layer: around the phone, add 4–6 compact glassmorphism chips with Korean labels like “보안 알림 ON”, “수수료 0원”, “간편 인증”, “자동 저축”, “평점 4.8”, and “누적 1,200만 다운로드”.
5. Trust cards area (lower-mid 20%): place {포인트 박스} as three separate rounded cards, evenly spaced, each card visually distinct but matching the same grid rhythm. Include small icons for shield, chart, and transfer; add short supporting captions such as “매일 쓰는 계좌를 더 똑똑하게”, “소비 흐름을 한눈에”, “목표 저축 자동 추천”.
6. CTA area (bottom 15%): place {CTA·인센티브} as a high-contrast action block, larger than the trust cards, with a button-like emphasis suitable for app download or signup conversion. Include a realistic button label in Korean such as “지금 앱 설치하기”, a promo code strip “PROMO CODE: FIN2026”, and an incentive note “신규 가입 혜택은 조건 충족 시 제공”.
7. Download and support details: add a small QR code placeholder box labeled “QR로 바로 설치”, tiny App Store / Google Play style badges, support line “고객센터 1599-0000”, and footer disclaimer “자세한 조건 및 유의사항은 앱에서 확인하세요.”
8. Color integration: apply {컬러 팔레트} consistently across headline accents, floating chips, cards, CTA, chart UI, QR frame, and small divider lines so the poster feels like one unified fintech ad system in {비율} vertical format.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: Pretendard or Noto Sans KR, headline in ExtraBold 72–88px equivalent, body/cards in Medium 28–34px equivalent, CTA in Bold 34–42px equivalent, footer/legal micro text in Regular 13–16px equivalent.
- Use crisp, modern Korean type with slightly condensed tracking for the headline, clear hierarchy for campaign label/date/service descriptor, and generous padding inside cards.
- Color palette: follow {컬러 팔레트}; use bright white or very pale cool gray as the base, with one strong brand accent color, secondary tint colors for chart/payment details, and dark charcoal text for contrast.
- Border/shadow: rounded cards with 16–20px radius, soft drop shadow 0px 10px 24px at 14% opacity, subtle inner highlight on CTA, delicate glassmorphism edge highlights on floating chips.
- Add realistic fintech poster production details: fine background grain, faint grid lines, translucent geometric shapes, small divider rules, app-install badge blocks, QR frame, and footer information row.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: Canon EOS R5 with 85mm f/1.2 product-shot look, iPhone-style mockup rendered like a premium app launch poster, slightly elevated front view, shallow depth cue focused on phone glass and CTA elements.
- Lighting: studio softbox from upper-left at 45° with gentle fill from right, clean specular control on the phone glass, realistic reflective edges on the device frame, soft shadow under floating cards.
- Color grade: crisp fintech palette with bright clean whites, saturated brand accent, cool neutral grays, high clarity edges, subtle premium contrast, and polished commercial retouching.
- Texture and realism: include a refined matte background surface, faint paper-like poster grain, small screen reflections, dimensional card shadows, and believable UI density appropriate for a real Korean app advertisement.

[6. MOOD]
Premium Korean fintech campaign poster — feels like a polished Toss / KakaoBank style launch ad with a trustworthy, energetic, conversion-focused editorial finish. The image should feel ready for an Instagram Story ad, subway digital signage, or app-install landing banner.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: the following strings must appear exactly and clearly in the rendered image: {헤드라인}, {앱·서비스}, {포인트 박스}, {CTA·인센티브}.
- Additional Korean text in the image should be short, readable, and finance-app appropriate, including examples such as “오늘의 금융 루틴”, “2026.05.01–05.31”, “이체 완료”, “잔액 2,480,000원”, “이번 달 소비 분석”, “보안 알림 ON”, “QR로 바로 설치”, and “지금 앱 설치하기”.
- App UI in the phone mockup must clearly show transfer completion, account balance, and chart elements.
- Keep composition balanced and advertisement-like, with the phone mockup as the hero, the trust cards as supporting information, and the CTA/download details as the clear conversion endpoint.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters

studio:prompts3:ours-991.content:
[INPUT]
- language: Korean
- output_size: 1024x1536

[1. PURPOSE]
헬스·피트니스 앱을 홍보하는 세로형 앱 광고 포스터.
운동 루틴, 칼로리 추적, 체중 변화, 무료 체험 혜택, 앱 다운로드 동선을 한 화면에서 즉시 이해시키는 퍼포먼스 마케팅 비주얼.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- 전체 레이아웃: 상단 브랜드·헤드라인 20%, 중앙 hero 48%, 하단 데이터 카드·CTA 26%, 하단 법적 고지와 QR 영역 6%로 분할.
- 최상단에는 {앱명} 로고타입, 별점 {평점}, “누적 사용자 {사용자수}” 같은 신뢰 요소를 작게 배치해 실제 앱 광고처럼 보이게 한다.
- 중앙 hero는 {hero}를 가장 크게 배치한다. 앱 화면 mockup은 전면 스마트폰 2장으로 구성하고, 운동 중인 사람의 측면 컷을 뒤쪽 또는 오른쪽에 겹쳐 배치해 에너지와 사용 맥락을 만든다.
- 배경은 단단한 다크 톤 플랫 기반에 미세한 입자감, 흐릿한 네온 그린 라이트 링, 얇은 운동 트래킹 라인 그래픽을 추가해 디지털 피트니스 광고의 깊이를 만든다.
- {앱·기능}, {헤드라인}, {CTA·다운로드}, {인포 박스}, {컬러 팔레트}, {프로모션코드}, {QR레이블}, {해시태그}, {약관문구}가 실제 광고 소재처럼 계층적으로 읽히게 한다.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Header area (top 20%): 왼쪽 상단에 {앱명} 앱 아이콘과 로고타입을 넣고, 오른쪽에는 {평점} / {사용자수}를 작은 pill 배지로 배치한다. 그 아래 {헤드라인}을 가장 크게 배치하고, 굵은 한글 타이포와 짧은 영문 강조가 섞인 광고 문구처럼 보이게 한다.
- Sub headline / feature line: 헤드라인 아래에 {앱·기능}을 한 줄 기능 설명으로 넣고, “AI 루틴 추천 · 식단 기록 · 체중 그래프”처럼 점 구분자로 실제 앱 소개 문구처럼 구성한다.
- Main hero area (middle 48%): {hero}를 핵심 시각으로 배치한다. 전면 스마트폰 mockup에는 홈 대시보드, 주간 체중 그래프, 운동 영상 썸네일, 식단 카드, 칼로리 링을 선명한 UI 카드로 보여준다. 옆의 인물 컷은 러닝 또는 스쿼트 준비 자세의 자연스러운 운동 장면으로 구성한다.
- Feature info area (lower-middle): {인포 박스} 3개를 작은 카드로 정렬해, 각 카드에 숫자가 가장 먼저 읽히도록 굵은 숫자 + 짧은 설명 구조로 만든다. 카드에는 작은 아이콘, 진행 바, 전일 대비 화살표를 넣어 데이터 앱 느낌을 강화한다.
- CTA footer (bottom 26%): {CTA·다운로드}를 네온 그린 버튼형 CTA로 크게 배치하고, 바로 아래에 iOS·Android 스토어형 배지, {프로모션코드}, “지금 시작하면 맞춤 루틴 자동 생성” 서브카피를 넣는다.
- QR / micro info strip: 우측 하단에는 QR 코드 박스와 {QR레이블}을 넣고, 좌측 하단에는 {해시태그}와 {약관문구}를 작은 글씨로 배치한다.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: Pretendard ExtraBold for headline, Pretendard SemiBold for CTA and info cards, Noto Sans KR Medium for subcopy; headline 72–88px 느낌, body 24–32px 느낌, 숫자 30–40px 느낌, micro text 14–18px 느낌.
- Color palette: {컬러 팔레트}를 유지하되, 네온 그린 #A6FF4D, 차콜 #1C1F24, 화이트 #F7F8FA, 코랄 #FF6B5E를 핵심으로 사용한다.
- Border/shadow: 앱 mockup과 카드에는 8px radius, soft drop shadow 0 12px 28px rgba(0,0,0,0.22), CTA 버튼은 더 강한 그림자로 눌러보고 싶은 클릭감을 준다.
- UI accents: 얇은 라인 아이콘, 작은 진행 바, 원형 칼로리 링, 주간 그래프, 체크리스트, 운동 타이머, 작은 알림 배지를 사용해 피트니스 앱 특유의 데이터 중심 디자인을 강조한다.
- Realistic ad details: 앱 아이콘, 별점 배지, 사용자 수, 프로모션 코드, QR 다운로드 박스, 스토어형 다운로드 배지, 하단 약관 문구가 모두 실제 모바일 앱 광고처럼 자연스럽게 포함되어야 한다.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: 85mm f/1.8 portrait look for the person cut, combined with clean product-render style framing for the app UI; overall composition should feel like a premium mobile app launch ad.
- Lighting: studio softbox key light from upper-left at 45°, subtle fill from right, crisp specular edge on the person cut, clean highlights on glass phone mockups and UI cards.
- Color grade: dark charcoal base with neon green highlights, clean white UI surfaces, small coral accent points, high contrast, controlled neon bloom around CTA and tracking-line graphics.

[6. MOOD]
Premium fitness app launch campaign — Apple-style product ad meets Nike training performance aesthetic, with a realistic Korean mobile performance ad finish.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: "매일 30분, 6주 후 새 몸." / "오늘 1,420 kcal" / "이번주 -1.2kg" / "60일째 연속" / "iOS·Android 다운로드" / "첫 7일 무료"
- Include realistic ad microcopy: "별점 4.8" / "누적 120만 다운로드" / "프로모션 코드: START7" / "QR로 10초 만에 시작" / "#오늘운동완료 #6주챌린지"
- The app UI must look like a real mobile app mockup with readable Korean labels, graph numbers, food card titles, workout timer, and progress bars.
- Body proportions must remain natural and athletic; facial expression, limbs, fingers, and workout posture must be anatomically believable.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]

- Broken Korean characters
- Sexualized fitness pose or revealing emphasis
- Unauthorized celebrity composites

K-pop comeback D-countdown card for Instagram, a square promotional graphic announcing the day count before a comeback.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Center composition with the main hero visual occupying about 58% of the frame, with a strong title zone at the top, a countdown/date zone in the lower third, and social-feed UI details around the edges.
- Background is a polished comeback poster surface: deep dark base with subtle neon glow, faint grain, glossy reflections, smoky light streaks, small holographic shapes, star glints, and layered promo-card textures that support the concept.
- Build a mobile-first hierarchy so {타이포} and {D-day} read instantly while surrounding details make the card feel like a real official comeback teaser post.
- Use {아티스트·컴백}, {D-day}, {hero 비주얼}, {타이포}, {컨셉}, {컬러 팔레트}, and {비율} as layout-driving placeholders.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1) Top header band: place {아티스트·컴백} in a compact but bold title zone, aligned center or slightly upper-center, with a crisp promotional-poster structure. Add a small label such as "COMEBACK COUNTDOWN", "NEW ERA", or "2026.05.01 18:00 KST" as a realistic promo metadata line.
2) Main hero area (middle 55-60%): place {hero 비주얼} as the visual anchor, either a dramatic silhouette or a stylized concept image with sharp editorial subject separation, glossy cutout edges, rim glow, and fashion-poster depth.
3) Countdown focal text: render {D-day} as the largest typographic element, layered near the hero or lower center so it feels like the key announcement. Add a short Korean companion label such as "컴백까지" or "드디어 공개" in smaller type.
4) Supporting type block: place {타이포} directly beneath or beside the countdown text in a stacked hierarchy, keeping album name and date information compact and legible. Include realistic short promo blurbs like "오늘 밤 6시", "콘셉트 포토 공개", "알림 ON".
5) Concept treatment: apply {컨셉} through background effects, edge lighting, holographic stickers, cropped lyric-like microtext, starburst accents, small arrows, and translucent glass panels so the whole card feels like a unified comeback-era teaser.
6) Social card details: add a tiny Instagram-style handle such as "@official_artist", hashtags like "#컴백 #D_DAY #KPOP", small save/share/heart micro icons, and a subtle page indicator "1/3" or "COUNTDOWN CARD" near the bottom edge.
7) Color system: build the full palette from {컬러 팔레트}, with high contrast between background and text for social-feed readability.
8) Final framing: keep {비율} as a square poster composition with safe mobile cropping, energetic symmetry, and a finished entertainment-agency promotional layout.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use Pretendard ExtraBold or SUIT Heavy for the countdown, with Noto Sans KR SemiBold for supporting text; headline size should feel poster-like and mobile-first, with tight tracking for impact.
- Add secondary typography layers: condensed English promo labels, short Korean teaser captions, tiny credit text such as "PHOTO · CONCEPT · TEASER", and micro metadata aligned along the side or bottom.
- Color palette: derive from {컬러 팔레트}; support with deep charcoal #111111, near-black #0B0B10, electric violet #7C3AED, neon cyan #22D3EE, hot pink #FF4FD8, and off-white #F5F1EA when contrast is needed.
- Border/shadow: use a soft outer glow and layered drop shadow, about 4px y-offset, 14px blur, 18% opacity, to separate text and hero from the background. Add thin translucent framing lines, glassmorphism panels, sticker shadows, and subtle light leaks for a premium comeback-card finish.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: editorial poster look inspired by a 50mm f/1.8 portrait setup or a 85mm f/1.4 beauty shot, with crisp subject separation and shallow depth-of-field styling.
- Lighting: studio key light from upper-left at 45° with a faint neon rim from the right, plus subtle backlight to outline the silhouette and typography layers.
- Color grade: dark cinematic base with neon accent grading, using cool blacks, saturated accent color, controlled highlights, glossy skin/fabric reflections where relevant, and realistic printed-poster texture for a polished comeback teaser feel.

[6. MOOD]
High-impact K-pop comeback teaser — music-show countdown poster meets fashion-editorial album promo, with the authenticity of a real Instagram announcement card from an entertainment label.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: the following verbatim strings must appear correctly in the rendered image when used by the generator: {아티스트·컴백}, {D-day}, {타이포}, {컨셉}
- Include short readable Korean promo text such as "컴백까지", "오늘 밤 6시", "콘셉트 포토 공개", "알림 ON", plus realistic social details like "@official_artist" and "#컴백 #D_DAY".
- Keep the composition square and poster-like, with the countdown clearly readable at a glance.
- Typography must remain sharp, clean, and properly aligned; no broken Korean characters.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]

- Broken Korean characters

[1. PURPOSE]
K-pop fan sign event / mini concert announcement poster, vertical A4-style promotional layout for fandom sharing and ticket/event notice.
Create a real, content-rich event poster with bold Korean headline typography, a dynamic hero visual, practical event information, ticketing details, sponsor/organizer strip, small production credits, and decorative concert graphics that feel like a polished K-pop agency promotion.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Top area (about 18%): energetic headline block centered, with {아티스트·이벤트} as the artist/event label and {헤드라인} as the primary focus. Add small realistic labels such as "FAN SIGN & MINI CONCERT", "2026 SPECIAL EVENT", "VOL.247", and a compact date tag like "2026.05".
- Middle hero zone (about 46%): {hero 이미지} placed as the central visual anchor, treated like a studio-shot idol promo image, luminous silhouette, album-jacket graphic, or stage teaser art. Surround it with layered light beams, soft confetti, heart stickers, starbursts, holographic ticket shapes, glow rings, and subtle fanlight motifs in {컬러 팔레트}.
- Lower information zone (about 26%): {일시·장소} and {당첨·예매} arranged in stacked event notice panels. Include realistic poster details: "일시", "장소", "예매", "당첨자 발표", "입장 안내", "문의 @fanevent_kr", "티켓 오픈 D-7", "좌석 랜덤 배정".
- Footer / sponsor area: add a narrow organizer and sponsor strip with small Korean text such as "주최: STAR LIVE", "주관: FANLINK", "협찬: K-POP STORE", "문의: 02-1234-5678", plus a small barcode/ticket-number area like "TICKET NO. 0526-247".
- Background: premium printed poster surface with soft paper grain, subtle ink texture, pastel-to-white gradient wash, holographic shimmer, stage-light haze, and decorative accents using {컬러 팔레트}.
- Spacing and framing: strong vertical hierarchy for a 1024x1536 portrait poster, with layered editorial alignment, crisp readable text blocks, realistic print-safe edges, and an energetic fandom promotional composition.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1) Header zone: place {아티스트·이벤트} in a compact supporting line, then set {헤드라인} as the dominant masthead in bold Korean display type. Add small supporting text around it: "팬싸·미니콘 포스터", "아티스트", "헤드라인", "FAN EVENT GUIDE", and "2026년 5월호".
2) Hero zone: render {hero 이미지} large and centered, either as a high-gloss fandom-color silhouette, idol-style promo portrait crop, emblem-style concert graphic, or album-cover-inspired stage visual. Add believable concert lighting, glow edges, reflected highlights, fanlight icons, small floating hearts, sparkle stickers, and a few ribbon-like graphic shapes in {컬러 팔레트}.
3) Schedule block: place {일시·장소} in a clearly boxed information area, using strong numeric hierarchy and short Korean labels. Include visible microcopy such as "일시", "장소", "입장 18:00", "공연 19:00", "현장 확인 필수", while keeping the supplied placeholder content exact.
4) Ticket / participation block: place {당첨·예매} in a separate lower notice strip formatted like a real event bulletin. Include "예매", "당첨자 발표", "응모 기간", "1인 1매", "신분증 지참", "티켓 오픈 D-7", and small QR/barcode-style graphic elements as decorative ticketing marks.
5) Accent system: use thin divider lines, dot markers, metallic gold rules, diagonal sticker tags, star/spark accents, tiny hearts, fan chant dots, and stage spotlight arcs to reinforce a K-pop mini concert poster feel.
6) Footer balance: include a realistic credit line and sponsor row at the bottom: "DESIGN CREDIT: FAN PROMO TEAM", "PHOTO / ART: {hero 이미지}", "COLOR: {컬러 팔레트}", "RATIO: {비율}", plus small organizer/sponsor text and a barcode-like ticket area.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: Pretendard ExtraBold for headline, Pretendard SemiBold for section labels, Noto Sans KR for body details; headline very large and sharp, event info medium, microcopy small but legible. Use mixed Korean/English event-poster typography with bold condensed numerals for dates.
- Color palette: {컬러 팔레트} plus clean white, soft black, metallic gold, and light holographic highlights. Use the fandom color as the main accent, white as the poster base, and gold for premium event dividers, badges, and ticket marks.
- Border/shadow: thin white or gold rules, soft drop shadow 4px y-offset, 12px blur, 15% opacity on hero and key blocks; add realistic print layering, small sticker shadows, glossy highlights, and subtle paper texture without heavy bevel effects.
- Text density: make the poster feel like a real event announcement by including headline, date/time, venue, ticketing, announcement notices, sponsor strip, barcode/ticket number, and tiny production credits.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: Canon EOS R5 with 85mm f/1.8 portrait-style framing for the hero artwork feel, with poster-clean depth separation; if graphic-based, emulate a studio promo shoot crop with centered emphasis and realistic lens compression.
- Lighting: concert-stage key light from upper-left with a soft rim from the right, plus gentle glow around the hero element, colored backlights, faint haze, and small specular highlights on sticker/ticket graphics.
- Color grade: white + fandom pastel + gold highlight grade, with crisp contrast, controlled saturation, soft skin-or-illustration rendering for the hero, and a polished K-pop promotional finish.
- Print realism: show slight paper grain, ink density variation, clean vector-like text edges, subtle halftone or holographic shimmer in accent areas, and a professional poster layout suitable for online sharing.

[6. MOOD]
Modern K-pop agency announcement poster — polished fan event promo sheet with high-energy stage teaser atmosphere, realistic ticketing information, fandom celebration details, and a premium mini concert / fan sign announcement feeling similar to a showcase bulletin or music program event poster.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: 반드시 다음 문구가 정확히 보여야 함: "팬싸·미니콘 포스터", "아티스트", "헤드라인", "일시", "예매", "컬러".
- Verbatim content fields must appear exactly as supplied through placeholders: {아티스트·이벤트}, {헤드라인}, {일시·장소}, {hero 이미지}, {당첨·예매}, {컬러 팔레트}, {비율}.
- Add realistic Korean poster microtext where space allows: "FAN SIGN & MINI CONCERT", "2026 SPECIAL EVENT", "입장 18:00 / 공연 19:00", "당첨자 발표", "티켓 오픈 D-7", "문의 @fanevent_kr", "주최: STAR LIVE", "주관: FANLINK", "TICKET NO. 0526-247".
- Typography must be clean and sharp; all Korean characters must be correctly rendered with no broken glyphs or spacing errors.
- Maintain a vertical poster hierarchy with the headline dominant, hero centered, event information blocks clearly separated, and sponsor/ticket details visible near the bottom.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]

[1. PURPOSE]
Cinematic K-pop music video still, portrait poster frame, designed like a single dramatic MV scene for social sharing, comeback teaser artwork, and vertical key visual promotion.
High-impact film still with emotional tension, built from {곡·아티스트} and {장면}, enriched with believable set details, atmospheric texture, and compact MV-poster information.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Main subject: {인물} placed slightly off-center in a vertical 1024x1536 frame, occupying about 45–55% of the height, with expressive posture and enough surrounding cinematic environment to tell a story.
- Scene setting: {장면} rendered as a realistic cinematic location, with visible depth layers in foreground, midground, and background; include natural location details such as wet pavement, window reflections, cables, signs, fabric, metal railings, vehicle lights, room objects, or street textures where appropriate.
- Framing: strong leading lines, asymmetrical composition, controlled headroom, and foreground elements that create depth without blocking the face or key silhouette.
- Background treatment: dark, moody environment with location-specific set dressing, soft haze, practical lights, reflected highlights, and production-like realism.
- Poster layer: integrate a compact teaser-title system directly over the still, including a small top label, main song/artist credit, release-time line, TAKE number, and tiny production credit text in Korean.
- Atmosphere: match the emotional tone of {연출 결} through spacing, posture, weather, light direction, expression, and scene tension.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Hero subject area: {인물} shown as the clear visual focus, with expressive body language and cinematic silhouette; preserve facial readability, natural skin texture, and strong emotional presence.
2. Scene anchor: {장면} establishes the narrative context with authentic set dressing, architectural detail, props, signage, vehicle/interior cues, weather traces, or lived-in surface textures depending on the location.
3. Motion cue: introduce subtle visual energy such as wind-blown hair, drifting haze, rain droplets, reflected neon, moving curtain fabric, road mist, lens streaks, or slight camera motion blur inspired by {카메라}.
4. Lighting structure: use contrast to carve out the subject from the background, with practical highlights, edge light, reflective surfaces, and deep shadow separation.
5. Color mood: apply {컬러 그레이딩} consistently across skin tones, shadows, highlights, signage, wardrobe, and atmospheric haze so the frame feels like a unified music-video still.
6. MV teaser typography: add believable poster details such as “MV 스틸컷”, “오늘 밤 6시 공개”, “TAKE 03”, “출연 {인물}”, “촬영 {카메라}”, and a small bottom credit strip, arranged like polished K-pop promotional key art.
7. Cinematic polish: finish with film grain, lens bloom, halation, subtle vignette, dust specks, realistic depth-of-field behavior, and highlight roll-off; the image should feel like a frame extracted from a feature-grade MV sequence.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use a compact movie-poster title lockup in Pretendard SemiBold or Noto Sans KR Bold, 28–44px equivalent for the main Korean line, with 10–16px equivalent micro-credit text; keep the title and credits integrated into the image like real MV teaser artwork.
- Color palette: derive from {컬러 그레이딩}, using teal #2D6F73, amber #C88A3A, deep charcoal #111111, muted blue #5A6F8F, and desaturated skin-friendly neutrals.
- Graphic details: allow subtle film leader marks, tiny frame numbers, barcode-like teaser strip, production-credit line, light leaks, and small Korean release labels, all secondary to the subject.
- Border/shadow: subtle soft vignette around edges, mild film-grain texture, gentle halation, and a restrained drop shadow only if needed for text readability or subject separation; avoid clean app-like UI borders.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: {카메라}; 35mm film look with a 50mm or 85mm cinematic lens, shallow-to-medium depth of field, anamorphic-style horizontal flares when relevant, and a portrait-oriented frame crop.
- Lighting: dramatic key light from one side at 45°, supported by a weak fill and practical back/rim light; use either night streetlight, neon spill, car headlights, hallway fluorescents, stage spill, or dawn window light depending on {장면}.
- Color grade: match {컬러 그레이딩} with teal-orange contrast, desaturated noir shadows, or blue-hour coolness; preserve highlight roll-off, realistic skin tonality, textured blacks, and believable reflected color.

[6. MOOD]
K-drama music film still — Park Chan-wook / Wong Kar-wai emotional tension with a polished K-pop MV teaser aesthetic, dramatic but believable, glossy yet tactile.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: render clear Korean text exactly as short teaser credits: “곡 {곡·아티스트}”, “장면 {장면}”, “연출 {연출 결}”, “출연 {인물}”, “촬영 {카메라}”, “톤 {컬러 그레이딩}”, “{비율}”.
- Additional Korean teaser text may include: “MV 스틸컷”, “오늘 밤 6시 공개”, “TAKE 03”, “CINEMA VERSION”, “비하인드 컷”, “감정의 끝에서”.
- Composition invariants: single-scene cinematic still, no collage or multi-panel layout, no extra characters stealing focus, and no distorted anatomy.
- Visual consistency: preserve the exact filmic mood implied by the chosen {연출 결}, {카메라}, and {컬러 그레이딩} values while keeping all poster text secondary to the cinematic subject.

[1. PURPOSE]
K-pop member profile sheet, 5-cut set for group introduction and social promotion.
Vertical editorial profile layout with one cinematic group hero and five individual member profile panels, designed to look like a real entertainment agency press-kit page, fan magazine insert, or comeback introduction sheet.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Overall framing: one top hero section plus five subordinate portrait panels arranged in a polished vertical sheet layout, with clear panel hierarchy, consistent gutters, and a strong reading order from group identity to individual member details.
- Subject placement: the group hero occupies the upper 28–32% of the frame, while the five member profiles fill the remaining area in a structured grid or evenly spaced horizontal sequence according to {레이아웃} and {비율}.
- Header and metadata: include a compact title band above or overlapping the hero with realistic editorial details such as "K-POP PROFILE", "VOL.05", "2026.05", "DEBUT DOSSIER", and a small agency-style credit line "PHOTO BY STUDIO WAVE".
- Background treatment: unified background surface matched to {컬러 팔레트}, with tactile studio backdrop texture, soft paper grain, faint gradient lighting, subtle tape marks, printed registration ticks, or glossy laminate reflections that make the sheet feel physically designed.
- Spacing and framing: maintain precise alignment and clear separation between panels; each member panel should include room for name, role, short stat line, and one small decorative tag without covering key facial features.
- Use {그룹·멤버 수}, {레이아웃}, {컨셉}, {타이포}, {의상·헤어}, {컬러 팔레트}, {비율} as customizable placeholders.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1) Hero area: place a cohesive group image or main collective portrait in the upper section, centered and slightly larger than the member panels, with editorial symmetry, coordinated poses, and a premium magazine casting-spread feel. Add a small caption such as "GROUP CUT / NEW PROFILE RELEASE" and Korean copy "새로운 시즌, 다섯 개의 시선".
2) Member panels: show five individual portraits below or beside the hero, each panel treated as a separate profile tile with matching crop scale, consistent headroom, and identical styling logic. Each tile may include a tiny role badge such as "LEADER", "VOCAL", "DANCE", "RAP", "VISUAL" paired with Korean labels like "리더", "보컬", "댄스", "랩", "비주얼".
3) Identity text layer: position each member’s English name and Korean subtitle near the portrait edge or in a caption band, ensuring legibility without covering key facial features. Example rendered names may include "HARIN 하린", "YUNA 유나", "SION 시온", "MINA 민아", "ROA 로아" with short captions such as "맑은 보컬", "퍼포먼스", "무대 에너지", "감성 랩", "센터 포커스".
4) Profile details: add small realistic profile-card microtext in each panel, such as "BIRTH 05.12", "HEIGHT 168", "POSITION MAIN VOCAL", "FAVORITE COLOR BLUE", plus Korean mini-copy like "오늘의 키워드: 반짝임" or "무대 위의 온도". Keep the microtext believable and arranged as printed design information.
5) Layout rhythm: use repeated panel borders, consistent spacing, small page markers, divider rules, index numbers "01–05", and a clear reading order from top to bottom so the sheet feels like an actual agency profile catalog page.
6) Style integration: keep the group and all five portraits visually coherent through the same lighting, color balance, wardrobe language, hair styling, and makeup finish based on {컨셉} and {의상·헤어}, so the sheet reads as one unified K-pop profile set.
7) Social/promo details: include a small handle such as "@newwave.official", a campaign tag "#데뷔프로필 #멤버소개", a tiny QR-like code block, a barcode-style catalog strip, page indicator "PROFILE 01/01", and a small footer line "© 2026 PROFILE ARCHIVE" for realistic promotional context.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use Pretendard Bold or Noto Sans KR SemiBold for Korean captions, paired with a clean sans-serif English name line in medium weight; name size should be slightly larger than subtitle size, with crisp anti-aliased edges and believable print registration.
- Color palette: match {컬러 팔레트}; if no palette is specified, use an idol-editorial range such as charcoal #1F1F1F, soft ivory #F4F0E8, cool gray #B8BDC6, and one refined accent tone for badges, dividers, stickers, or highlight rules.
- Border/shadow: thin 1px panel dividers, subtle soft shadow 4px y-offset, 12px blur, 12–15% opacity, plus occasional glossy label edges or translucent overlay strips for depth.
- Graphic treatment: polished sheet design with layered editorial elements, profile badges, caption bands, index numbers, sticker-like tags, thin rule lines, and magazine-style footer credits while keeping portraits dominant.
- Detail density: include enough small real-world information to make the sheet look designed and published: issue/date label, member stats, caption snippets, agency-style credits, page number, and promotional handle.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: editorial portrait look with 85mm f/1.8 for individual members and a 50mm f/2.0 or 70mm equivalent for the group hero, natural facial proportions, sharp focus on eyes.
- Lighting: controlled studio softbox at 45° from upper-left with gentle fill from front-right; keep shadows soft and consistent across all five portraits, with catchlights visible and believable skin texture.
- Color grade: unified K-pop editorial grade with neutral skin tones, slightly cool shadows, and restrained saturation aligned to {컨셉}; maintain coherent wardrobe and hair color harmony with {컬러 팔레트}.
- Surface/material feel: high-end promotional print aesthetic, like a polished entertainment agency profile sheet, magazine casting spread, or limited fan-kit insert printed on satin-coated paper.
- Realism cues: add subtle paper fibers, print halftone at very small text edges, mild lens compression, natural fabric folds, realistic hair flyaways, makeup detail, jewelry glints, and faint reflected highlights on glossy caption strips.

[6. MOOD]
K-pop agency profile editorial — polished entertainment press kit feel with confident debut energy, magazine-sheet rhythm, refined idol styling, and realistic promotional details that make the image feel like a finished collectible profile page.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: the following placeholder labels must appear exactly as intended in the rendered image when used as visible template labels: "그룹·멤버 수", "레이아웃", "컨셉", "타이포", "의상·헤어", "컬러 팔레트", "비율".
- Render Korean cover/profile copy clearly, including short strings such as "새로운 시즌, 다섯 개의 시선", "멤버 프로필", "데뷔 프로필", "오늘의 키워드", "무대 위의 온도", and "프로필 아카이브".
- If member name captions are present, render all Korean characters cleanly with no broken glyphs; English and Korean names should align naturally within each profile tile.
- Keep the composition as a 5-cut profile sheet with one group hero section and five individual member sections; do not change the panel count.
- Faces, hands, and body proportions must remain natural and anatomically correct; no distorted idol features.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]

- Broken Korean characters
- Celebrity composites / unauthorized likeness

[1. PURPOSE]
K-pop solo debut teaser poster, vertical A4-style promotional key visual for a first solo release announcement.
Fashion-forward idol teaser designed for social sharing, music-platform reveal posts, street-poster realism, and fan repost culture, with strong title hierarchy, countdown emphasis, and credible event-poster details.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Subject placement: {hero 컷} should occupy the central 55–65% of the frame, with the upper 18% reserved for headline typography and the lower 14% reserved for the countdown and release block.
- Background treatment: build a layered concept set that matches {컨셉}, using visible surfaces such as painted studio wall, reflective floor, fabric sweep, chrome panel, paper-poster wall, light leaks, concert-ticket scraps, lyric-sheet fragments, or subtle stage equipment silhouettes that support the idol debut atmosphere.
- Framing direction: poster should feel like a premium single-artist teaser sheet photographed for a real agency campaign, with the face or full body rendered as the clear hero and the surrounding typography, ticket labels, microcredits, and graphic marks locked to a strong vertical grid.
- Visual balance: keep {아티스트·데뷔} as the emotional anchor, while {타이포}, {카운트다운}, release information, showcase details, and supporting Korean blurbs create a stacked magazine-cover-meets-concert-poster hierarchy.
- Real poster details: include a small barcode or QR-style ticket block, issue-like label such as “TEASER POSTER 01”, date/time/venue line, ticket-open notice, sponsor/presenter strip, tiny copyright/production credit, and 2–3 short Korean feature blurbs related to the solo debut.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Top header zone (upper 18%): place the artist/debut line {아티스트·데뷔} as the primary identity statement, centered or slightly above center, with strong spacing. Add small supporting labels such as “SOLO DEBUT TEASER”, “POSTER 01”, “2026.06”, and a tiny credit line like “PHOTO / CREATIVE DIRECTION / STUDIO SESSION”.
2. Hero zone (mid 55–65%): render {hero 컷} as the dominant visual, with polished studio presentation, crisp silhouette separation, expressive pose, detailed wardrobe texture, stage-ready hair and makeup, and tangible set elements that match the chosen concept tone.
3. Typography zone: set {타이포} in a bold, high-contrast style that feels like a debut announcement, with English name emphasis and compact layout. Add 2–3 short Korean promo blurbs around the hero, for example “첫 솔로의 문이 열린다”, “새로운 이름, 새로운 장면”, “타이틀 트랙 공개”, keeping them readable and secondary to the main title.
4. Countdown zone (lower 14%): display {카운트다운} as the most readable secondary callout, using oversized numerals or release-date treatment with strong contrast. Include realistic release information such as “2026.06.15 MON 8PM”, “D-7”, “RELEASE”, or “COMING SOON”.
5. Event and ticket block: below or beside the countdown, add compact poster information such as “DEBUT SHOWCASE”, “서울 블루스퀘어 아이마켓홀”, “TICKET OPEN 2026.06.01 12PM”, “온라인 동시 생중계”, and a small barcode/QR-style rectangle for ticketing realism.
6. Sponsor and credit strip: near the bottom edge, add a believable presenter/sponsor area with small text like “Presented by STUDIO A”, “Media Partner K-MAG”, “Styling / Hair / Makeup / Photo”, and a tiny handle such as “@official_solo”, designed as microtypography rather than a major focal point.
7. Concept integration: reinforce {컨셉} through pose, wardrobe texture, set materials, props, lighting color, graphic overlays, and finishing details, so the image reads as one coherent debut campaign rather than a generic portrait.
8. Palette application: apply {컬러 팔레트} to the background, accent glow, poster markings, text color, shadows, small stickers, and ticket-block graphics, keeping the palette disciplined and consistent across all layout elements.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use Pretendard ExtraBold for modern Korean text, Noto Sans KR Bold for supporting labels, and a condensed Latin sans such as Bebas Neue or Anton for the name/countdown treatment; title size should be poster-large, with tight leading and controlled letter spacing.
- Korean text rendering: all Korean headline, date, venue, and ticket text must be crisp, correctly spaced, and printed like real poster typography, not decorative gibberish.
- Color palette: derive the entire layout from {컬러 팔레트}; if the concept is dark, bias toward charcoal, deep navy, black, and metallic gold accents; if neon, bias toward electric pink, cyan, violet, and graphite; if vintage, bias toward cream, sepia, muted burgundy, and warm brass.
- Poster graphic elements: use layered rectangular labels, diagonal accent bars, small starbursts, transparent tape marks, holographic sticker-like shapes, cropped lyric snippets, thin divider rules, date stamps, and production microtext to make the poster feel physically designed and campaign-ready.
- Border/shadow: use either a full-bleed poster edge or a very thin hairline border; add a soft drop shadow only if needed, about 4px y-offset, 12px blur, 15% opacity, to separate the hero from the background. Subtle paper grain, print texture, and edge wear are welcome if they suit {컨셉}.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: fashion-editorial studio look shot on a Hasselblad X2D 100C with an 85mm lens at f/2.8 for a portrait hero, or a 50mm lens at f/4 for a more graphic full-body teaser composition.
- Lighting: use controlled studio lighting with a key light from upper-left at roughly 45°, a subtle rim light from the opposite side for edge separation, and a gentle fill to preserve facial detail, costume texture, metallic accents, and printed poster elements.
- Color grade: finish with a cinematic editorial grade aligned to {컨셉}; use deep blacks and metallic highlights for dark luxury, soft warm neutrals for elegant vintage, saturated neon accents for cyber style, or muted cream-and-rose tones for warm magazine styling.
- Material realism: include realistic fabric sheen, skin detail, hair texture, jewelry reflections, printed-paper grain, soft floor reflection, and small light falloff so the image feels photographed and professionally composited rather than flat.

[6. MOOD]
Premium K-pop debut teaser — fashion magazine cover meets concert announcement poster, with the polished intensity of a Vogue Korea campaign visual and the excitement of a real agency countdown drop.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: 반드시 정확히 보여야 하는 문구: "솔로 가수 ○○ — 데뷔 미니 1집 / Coming Soon", "D-7 또는 2026.06.15 RELEASE", "한글·영문 정확".
- Required placeholder integration: {아티스트·데뷔}, {hero 컷}, {타이포}, {카운트다운}, {컨셉}, {컬러 팔레트}, and {비율} must remain visually reflected in the final poster concept.
- Additional small poster text may include: "DEBUT SHOWCASE", "2026.06.15 MON 8PM", "서울 블루스퀘어 아이마켓홀", "TICKET OPEN 2026.06.01 12PM", "온라인 동시 생중계", "@official_solo", "TEASER POSTER 01".
- Layout invariants: the hero must remain the single dominant focus, the countdown must be clearly legible, and the overall composition must feel like a legitimate idol solo debut teaser poster with real campaign typography, ticket details, credits, and balanced graphic density.
- Text handling: preserve the intended English/Korean mix cleanly; avoid garbling, mirrored letters, broken spacing, or unreadable microtype in headline, countdown, venue, ticket, and credit treatments.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters
- Unauthorized celebrity likeness composites or face-swapped real idols

[1. PURPOSE]
K-pop 5세대 digital album jacket cover for social and streaming use, square 1:1 layout with premium collectible-art direction.
Designed to feel like a modern K-pop comeback jacket with strong hero focus, typography-first branding, and believable physical-album packaging details such as edition marks, catalog code, release date, hype sticker, and small-print credits.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Square cover composition with a centered or slightly off-center hero occupying 58–65% of the frame, surrounded by layered album-package graphics, a clear top title zone, and a lower-third information zone for {타이포}.
- Background treatment should follow {컨셉 톤}: soft atmospheric gradient, tactile paper surface, glossy noir studio space, dreamlike Y2K set, or warm natural beige backdrop, depending on the selected concept.
- Add realistic album-jacket details: a small barcode or catalog label, compact release-date text, edition badge, track teaser sticker, and thin spine-credit style vertical text along one edge.
- The hero should match {hero 비주얼}, with styling, pose, accessories, hair, and makeup designed to support a high-end K-pop comeback jacket look.
- Use {아티스트·앨범} as the identity anchor, with the album name integrated as the primary visual hierarchy and supporting Korean text placed as collectible packaging copy.
- The overall palette must stay within {컬러 팔레트}, with careful color separation between subject, background, type, stickers, and foil-like accent elements.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1) Background layer: build a 1:1 album-jacket field that reflects {컨셉 톤}, using gradient lighting, studio backdrop, textured paper, glossy reflections, fabric folds, stickers, translucent shapes, or printed-package surfaces.
2) Hero layer: place {hero 비주얼} as the main focal point, centered or slightly off-center depending on the concept, with polished integrated portrait styling, refined hair detail, and natural skin texture.
3) Title layer: render {타이포} in a large, high-contrast hierarchy, positioned so it anchors the cover without covering the face or key styling details.
4) Packaging information layer: include {발매 정보}, {카탈로그 번호}, {크레딧 라인}, and a small vertical spine-credit text treatment that reads like a real album sleeve edge.
5) Sticker and track teaser layer: add {트랙 스티커} as a removable-style hype sticker, translucent label, circular foil sticker, or rectangular price-tag style label, integrated into the visual rhythm.
6) Palette accents: apply {컬러 팔레트} as selective accent color blocks, glow edges, shadow tints, ribbon strips, sticker outlines, or foil-like highlights to reinforce the comeback identity.
7) Finishing layer: add a premium jacket finish such as embossed title texture, glossy print sheen, faint film grain, pearlescent ink, holographic strip, or glitter-foil effect to make the square art feel physically collectible.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use bold modern K-pop display typography for the main album name, paired with a clean supporting sans-serif or light serif for the Korean subtitle and packaging copy; suggested fonts include Pretendard Bold, Noto Sans KR SemiBold, or Nanum Myeongjo depending on {컨셉 톤}.
- Keep the type sharp, fully legible, and integrated into the cover geometry; avoid decorative distortion that reduces readability.
- Include realistic microcopy hierarchy: main title, Korean subtitle, release date, catalog number, edition label, track teaser, and tiny production-credit line.
- Color palette must come from {컬러 팔레트}, with specific use of dusty pink, dark navy, vintage beige, champagne gold, silver, or neon glow accents as appropriate to the concept.
- Border/shadow: use a soft drop shadow with 4px y-offset, 12px blur, and about 15% opacity for the hero, stickers, type elements, or barcode label when separation from background is needed.
- If glitter, foil, holographic tape, or emboss is used, keep it restrained and premium, like an offset-print jacket detail rather than a toy-like sparkle effect.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: fashion-editorial portrait feel, shot like a 85mm f/1.4 or 50mm f/1.8 studio portrait depending on the hero setup; for group layouts, a 35mm lens look with controlled perspective is appropriate.
- Lighting: polished studio lighting with a large softbox at 45° from upper-left, subtle fill from front-right, and a faint rim light to separate hair and shoulders from the background.
- Color grade: choose a tightly controlled K-pop comeback grade matching {컨셉 톤}, such as dusty rose + silver, deep navy + cyan neon, warm beige + champagne gold, black + muted violet, or pearly white + soft lavender.
- Print realism: show subtle jacket-paper grain, laminated gloss, small dust specks, foil highlights, and ink-density variation so the cover feels like a photographed collectible album sleeve.

[6. MOOD]
Premium K-pop comeback album art — like a high-end SM/ADOR-era jacket photo mixed with Vogue Korea cover polish, Gen-Z collectible design language, and a limited-edition physical album package finish.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: 반드시 정확히 보여야 하는 문구: "{아티스트·앨범}", "{타이포}", "{발매 정보}", "{트랙 스티커}", "{카탈로그 번호}", "{크레딧 라인}".
- Render the added Korean packaging copy clearly, for example: "초회 한정반", "타이틀곡 포함 6곡", "2026.05.24 RELEASE", "VOL.01 / KJ-0524", "프로듀싱: 스튜디오 새벽".
- The square 1:1 framing must remain intact, with the hero never cropped awkwardly and the title never overlapping unreadable areas.
- Maintain precise K-pop jacket aesthetics: elegant styling, clean face proportions, premium wardrobe coordination, and no unnatural facial warping.
- If the concept includes a group, keep member proportions consistent, faces fully coherent, and styling unified across all members.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters
- Text gibberish or unreadable typography
- Celebrity composites or unauthorized real-person identity blending

[1. PURPOSE]
Korean sky landscape artwork, expansive square composition for calm wallpaper or social background.
A refreshing morning-sky scene with soft cumulus clouds, luminous daylight, and a thin realistic horizon layer, designed to feel spacious, serene, and naturally lived-in.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- The sky dominates about 75–80% of the square frame, with the horizon line placed low so the atmosphere feels broad and immersive.
- {주제} should read as the central atmosphere of the image: a bright blue morning sky, slow-moving cloud forms, and a peaceful open-air landscape beneath it.
- Add a low horizon strip with {하단 풍경 요소}: a very distant field, quiet waterline, or soft tree ridge with morning haze, kept small but physically believable.
- Clouds should be distributed with natural variation: larger cottony cumulus masses around the upper-middle and mid-right, smaller wisps drifting toward the left, all shaped by morning wind.
- Frame the composition as a square scenic postcard with a calm center of attention created by light, cloud volume, horizon glow, and subtle foreground atmosphere.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1) Sky field: build a broad blue sky gradient from deeper blue overhead to lighter blue near the horizon, with smooth tonal transition and subtle film-like grain.
2) Cloud layer: place soft, voluminous cumulus clouds across the upper-middle and mid-right areas; include faint feathered cloud edges and translucent thin cloud veils for realism.

5) Composition framing: apply {구도·앵글}, keeping the sky expansive while allowing the low landscape strip to anchor the scene naturally.

7) Output finish: preserve the photographic feel implied by {카메라·렌즈·필름}, including medium-format depth, fine grain, vivid transparency, and natural atmospheric softness.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: landscape-only image; do not design it as a poster, cover, or text layout.
- Color palette: {컬러 팔레트}, with supporting sky tones in #7DB9E8, #A9D8F5, pale cream highlights, and deeper cobalt accents near the top.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]

- Lighting: {조명·라이팅}, with soft diffuse highlights, mild golden rim light, and sunlight appearing gently wrapped by thin atmosphere.
- Color grade: fresh morning blue with warm gold-tinted cloud rims, Velvia-like saturation but still natural, airy, and believable.
- Detail level: realistic cloud geometry, subtle tonal depth in the sky, and softly resolved distant landscape detail rather than flat graphic shapes.

[6. MOOD]

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: 이미지 안에는 글자나 간판이 보이지 않는 자연 풍경으로 표현한다.

Designed to feel like a premium e-commerce product sheet for Coupang, Naver Smart Store, or Amazon-style marketplace presentation, with realistic marketplace UI labels, short Korean feature captions, panel tags, and product-detail information that make the image feel ready for an actual online listing.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Single product hero placement: the main product occupies the left 55–60% of the frame, while the right side is divided into a 2x2 grid of four smaller supporting views.
- Background treatment: bright white studio base #FFFFFF with subtle real contact shadows, faint paper-like tonal variation, and lightly separated panel areas so the product sheet feels photographed and designed rather than sterile.

- Use {카메라} for the entire series so the product surface detail remains crisp, sharp, and commercial.
- Use {비율} as the final canvas structure and panel distribution guide.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Hero area (left 55–60%): render {원본 제품} as the largest cutout, centered vertically, with a realistic studio contact shadow beneath and slightly behind it, keeping the original label, logo, material, finish, and surface details exactly intact. Add a small title-card label nearby in Korean, such as “메인 대표컷” and “선명한 실물 컬러”, sized like marketplace UI text.

Add a small callout line or dot marker pointing to a real existing edge, cap, seam, label area, or texture feature, with Korean text like “측면 라인” or “입체감 확인”.

[4. STYLE RULES]

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]

- Scene setting: {목업 장면} with lived-in location details from {장면 디테일}, using realistic materials such as matte wood grain, woven linen, ceramic tile, brushed metal, stone countertop, painted wall panel, or softly wrinkled bedding.
- Background treatment: {배경 무드} using soft daylight, subtle depth separation, visible surface tactility, and a believable everyday environment that supports the product story.
- Prop arrangement: {소품 톤} and {실사용 소품} arranged as if the product is genuinely being used, with layered heights, contact shadows, partial overlaps, and practical placement that does not cover the product label or key silhouette.
- Camera framing: {구도} with balanced asymmetry, product faces the viewer at a readable angle, edges remain comfortable inside the square crop, and the surrounding objects help guide attention back to the hero product.
- Context cue: include a small lifestyle cue such as {현장 텍스트} on a note, receipt, bookmark, coaster, calendar card, pouch tag, or phone screen near the product, never printed onto the product itself.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1) Hero zone: {원본 제품} is placed first and kept visually dominant, with the exact product shape, proportions, texture, surface finish, label, logo, branding, and any printed text preserved from the reference image.
2) Surface zone: build the scene on a location-appropriate surface for {목업 장면}, such as lightly textured oak, linen cloth, stone countertop, bathroom shelf laminate, cafe marble, or ceramic tray, with realistic contact shadows and small material imperfections.
3) Support props: add practical objects matching {실사용 소품}, such as a used notebook, laptop corner, folded towel, coffee cup with crema, spoon, candle, magazine page, linen napkin, skincare spatula, small tray, dried flower stem, receipt, or phone, positioned to tell a real-use story.
4) Environmental details: include subtle cues from {장면 디테일} and {계절감}, such as window-frame shadow, morning condensation on glass, fabric folds, ceramic speckles, handwritten memo, tiny crumbs, water droplets, opened book edge, or a soft reflection on polished stone.
5) Light behavior: use directional natural light that shapes the object cleanly, with soft falloff, gentle highlight rolloff, and realistic reflections appropriate to the product material.
6) Depth and spacing: create layered foreground, hero, and background zones so the image feels photographed in a real room; allow some props to be partially cropped at the edge for candid editorial realism while keeping the product fully readable.
7) Integration rule: the product must look physically placed in the scene, not pasted in; retain realistic shadows, reflections, occlusion, scale consistency, and edge softness consistent with the surface and lighting.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: no added typography on the product itself; if scene text appears on props, render it in clean Korean using Pretendard or Noto Sans KR Medium, small but readable, such as “오늘의 기록”, “오전 10:20”, “서촌 스튜디오”, “주말 루틴”, or {현장 텍스트}.
- Color palette: use {소품 톤} with tactile neutrals such as warm beige, mocha brown, soft cream, muted gray, clean white, pale sage, oatmeal linen, and muted charcoal, with accent colors borrowed from the original product.
- Border/shadow: subtle natural contact shadow under the product, roughly 4px y-offset, 14px blur, 12–18% opacity; avoid harsh outline or cutout halo.
- Finish: preserve original product surface detail exactly; do not smooth, repaint, re-label, or increase saturation unnaturally.
- Marketing usability: composition should work for {채널 용도}, with the product instantly recognizable at thumbnail size while still feeling like a premium lifestyle photograph.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: Sony A7R V with 35mm f/2.8 or equivalent, natural product-photography perspective with minimal distortion.
- Lighting: soft window light from upper-left at about 45°, gentle bounce fill from lower-right, with realistic ambient shadowing and mild specular control.
- Color grade: editorial warm-neutral grade with creamy whites, soft brown undertones, lightly lifted shadows, natural blacks, and a gentle magazine still-life finish.

[6. MOOD]
Indie boutique lifestyle product photo — Aesop / Kinfolk magazine spread aesthetic, practical, tactile, refined, and realistically lived-in rather than showroom-staged.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: any Korean text already present on the reference product must remain exact and fully legible, with no broken characters, no altered spelling, no invented words, and no warped logo or label text.
- Product fidelity: replicate the EXACT product from the reference image — preserve precise shape, proportion, texture, color, label, logo, branding, cap, lid, wrapper, paper grain, glass reflection, embossed mark, and any printed text.
- Scene-only change: replace ONLY the background, surface, props, and lighting; do not redesign, beautify, repackage, recolor, or invent any part of the product.
- Rendered scene text may appear only on separate props, for example “오늘의 기록”, “오전 10:20”, “서촌 스튜디오”, “주말 루틴”, “₩7,500”, “감사합니다”, or {현장 텍스트}; all Hangul must be clean, correctly spaced, and readable.
- Physical realism: all objects must cast believable shadows, sit naturally on the surface, match the same light direction, and maintain accurate scale relative to the hero product.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications / award badges
- Broken Korean characters or unreadable Hangul
- Celebrity composites or unauthorized face swaps
- Fabricated safety, legal, medical, or government compliance marks

[INPUT]

[1. PURPOSE]
1-2 English lines: High-end e-commerce cutout and premium studio re-photography for small home appliances and electronics, preserving the exact original product while upgrading the background, lighting, surface realism, and commercial presentation.
Square luxury product image for marketplace main images, online ads, product detail pages, and electronics launch visuals.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- {원본 제품} is the single hero object, occupying about 62% of the frame in {비율}, presented as a premium commercial product photograph rather than a flat mockup.
- {구도} should place the product with natural visual balance, keeping the full silhouette visible and uncropped while allowing a believable studio-photo stance.
- Background is a professional studio surface set by {배경 옵션}: a seamless sweep, softly curved backdrop, premium matte platform, faint acrylic reflection, or subtle tonal gradient that supports the product without changing it.
- Add realistic grounding through contact shadow, soft floor reflection, gentle ambient bounce, and tiny exposure falloff so the object feels physically photographed in a studio.
- Keep the silhouette edges crisp and preserve all product details, including tiny screws, buttons, vents, seams, material transitions, rubber feet, metallic bevels, glass, plastic, and satin finishes.
- {포트·로고 디테일} must remain clearly readable and correctly positioned, with no distortion from perspective, retouching, glare, or relighting.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Hero object pass: {원본 제품} rendered exactly as in the reference image, with original material finish, color, labeling, printed text, logo, ports, buttons, seams, scale cues, and manufacturing details preserved.
- Background pass: apply {배경 옵션} as a realistic premium studio environment, such as pure white marketplace sweep, warm gray tabletop, deep charcoal luxury set, brushed neutral surface, or softly graded commercial backdrop.
- Surface realism pass: include a believable tabletop or sweep-floor transition, subtle micro-texture, faint reflection beneath glossy or metallic products, and soft dust-free studio polish appropriate for high-end electronics.
- Lighting pass: {라이팅} should create controlled specular highlights on plastic, glass, metal, satin coating, screens, knobs, and edges, with natural shadow falloff and clean separation from the background.
- Angle and lens pass: {카메라} should reproduce a professional product-photo perspective, matching the source object’s proportions without redesigning the form or flattening the volume.
- Detail integrity pass: keep buttons, ports, vents, seams, labels, logos, surface text, panel gaps, LEDs, rubber feet, hinge lines, and connector geometry sharp and anatomically correct to the original product.
- Final cutout polish: remove unwanted original background spill while preserving true contour lines, natural edge highlights, transparent-looking gaps, hairline seams, and realistic contact shadow.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: do not add external ad copy or overlay typography; only preserve text already printed on the source product, including Korean, numbers, model labels, safety markings, and brand text.
- Color palette: use {배경 옵션} exactly as provided; if white, keep a premium #FFFFFF-to-light-gray studio sweep with neutral grayscale shadows; if dark, use deep charcoal #1A1A1A with restrained silver edge highlights and controlled black detail.
- Shadow and reflection: soft studio contact shadow with approximately 4px y-offset, 16px blur, 14% opacity as a base, plus physically plausible reflection or occlusion when the surface/material calls for it.
- Surface treatment: preserve matte-to-satin product finish, crisp specular control on plastic and metal parts, soft glow on glass or screen surfaces, and natural bevel highlights along edges.
- Commercial realism: allow subtle backdrop gradient, studio sweep curve, faint tabletop texture, and high-end retouching polish so the final image feels like a real product campaign shot.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: Phase One digital medium format look, 120mm macro, f/8, front-facing product repro perspective.
- Lighting: 3-light studio setup with key at 45° front-left, fill at low intensity front-right, and a thin rim light from rear-right to outline the product; add realistic bounce from the surface and controlled flags/reflections for glossy areas.
- Color grade: neutral commercial product grade with clean whites, controlled blacks, accurate material color reproduction, high micro-contrast on edges, and smooth tonal rolloff.

[6. MOOD]
Premium studio catalog product shot — Apple-style precision mixed with high-end marketplace clarity, realistic electronics advertising, refined material presence, and tactile studio depth.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: preserve every printed Korean character already present on the product exactly as in the reference image; do not invent or alter any Korean text.
- Preserve the exact product from the reference image: shape, proportion, texture, color, label, logo, branding, and all printed text must remain unchanged.
- Replace ONLY the background, lighting, surface grounding, and studio presentation; do not redesign, beautify into a different product, reinterpret, or add any new product features.
- All ports, buttons, seams, vents, LEDs, edges, logo placements, model numbers, icons, and material boundaries must match the reference image precisely.
- Maintain realistic physical scale and perspective: the product must look photographed on a premium studio set, not generated as a simplified icon or sterile flat cutout.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters

- Composition should feel like a premium Korean retail catalog shot: centered packshot clarity with enough surrounding tabletop context to make the product look real and photographed, not computer-flat.
- Optional accent detail: {소품 옵션} may appear as category-appropriate styling, such as fresh ingredients, ice cubes, a small glass, condensation droplets, a spoon, citrus slices, coffee beans, grains, herbs, or a folded napkin, placed around the base or side without covering the label.
- Maintain {비율} framing and a square 1024x1024 commercial product-image feel.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Hero product area (center 70%): {원본 제품} rendered as a precise cutout-quality product subject with clean edges, matching the reference shape and material finish, with no redesign.
- Label focus zone: the front label is fully visible, flat to camera, sharp enough to read every character; no perspective skew, warping, glare, or reflection that distorts Korean text.
- Background layer: realistic {배경} studio surface with a soft contact shadow, faint bounce light, and subtle material texture that supports the product without competing with the label.
- Accent layer: {소품 옵션} arranged naturally as small supporting food-and-beverage cues near the base or lateral edges, adding freshness, scale, and appetite appeal while keeping the product silhouette and printed text unobstructed.

- Color palette: use clean whites #FFFFFF / #F7F7F7, soft neutral gray #D9D9D9 for shadow, natural tabletop neutrals, and the product’s original packaging colors unchanged.
- Border/shadow: very soft realistic contact shadow, approximately 4px y-offset, 12px blur, 12–15% opacity, with additional faint ambient occlusion directly under the product for a real studio-photographed look.

- Lighting: {라이팅}; top key light with left-side fill, crisp label reveal, controlled speculars, studio-white environment, short soft shadow, and subtle bounce reflections from the tabletop.
- Color grade: neutral commercial product grade, clean whites and true-to-reference packaging tones, no warm tint or cinematic cast.
- Focus: label and front packaging tack-sharp from edge to edge, with only very gentle depth falloff on side props if present.
- Texture rendering: preserve realistic micro-textures such as paper grain, plastic seams, foil crinkles, condensation beads, embossed caps, printed ink edges, and transparent glass thickness where they exist in the reference.

- Broken Korean characters

Designed for marketplace detail pages, catalog thumbnails, premium product listing visuals, with realistic retail-spec annotations and close-up material storytelling.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Main subject: {원본 제품} must remain the exact photographed product, with no redesign; place it as the hero object across a 2-cut or 3-cut multi-panel layout depending on {레이아웃}.
- Panel arrangement: build a polished square catalog board with one larger hero view and supporting side/detail views; use refined panel dividers, small Korean angle labels, measurement-style guide marks, and subtle product information chips that feel like a premium shopping detail page.
- Background treatment: use {배경} as the base, primarily clean white / warm off-white studio paper with subtle paper grain, faint gray dividers, realistic contact shadows, and crisp product edges while preserving the product’s real material sheen.
- Category adaptation: match {카테고리} presentation logic by emphasizing shape, stitching, logo placement, sole structure, handle curves, leather grain, canvas weave, outsole texture, strap attachment, zipper pull, buckle hardware, or edge finishing as appropriate.
- Add a small catalog footer area with realistic micro text such as SKU-like code, size/angle notes, and a barcode-style block; keep it secondary so the product remains dominant.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Panel 1 (primary hero, about 45-50% visual weight): show {원본 제품} in a clean front or 3/4 angle with full silhouette visibility; keep proportions exact and place a short Korean label nearby such as “대표컷”, “FRONT 3/4”, or “메인 실루엣”.
- Panel 2 (supporting side view): show the same {원본 제품} from the most informative lateral angle, revealing profile thickness, strap fall, sole height, handle depth, or side seam construction; add small callout text such as “측면 라인”, “굽 높이”, “스트랩 구조”, or “사이드 쉐입”.
- Panel 3 (macro detail, when used): zoom into the most brand-relevant material detail such as stitching, logo embossing, buckle hardware, zipper pull, canvas weave, outsole texture, leather grain, or edge coating; make it physically faithful, sharp, and labeled “디테일 컷” or “소재 확대”.
- Edge handling: use precise masking around contours, with natural anti-aliased cutout edges, no halo, no background spill, and no artificial blur bleeding into the object boundary.
- Shadow logic: add a soft realistic contact shadow directly beneath the object in each panel, matching the object’s mass and direction of light under {라이팅}; shadows may vary subtly between hero, side, and macro panels for realism.
- Retail metadata: include 2-4 tiny Korean information chips that fit the product type, for example “컬러 확인”, “하드웨어”, “스티치”, “아웃솔”, “수납 라인”, “착화 각도”; include a small bottom caption line like “PRODUCT DETAIL SHEET · 2026 S/S · LOOK 03” without implying certification.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use Pretendard SemiBold / Medium for Korean labels, 18-28px for panel titles and 9-13px for micro metadata; dark charcoal #222222, medium gray #777777, and light gray #BDBDBD are preferred.
- Color palette: white #FFFFFF, soft gray #E9E9E9, charcoal #222222, warm paper white #FAFAF7, and the product’s original colors preserved exactly; no color shift away from the source.
- Border/shadow: refined 1px hairline gray dividers #EAEAEA, subtle rounded panel corners if appropriate, soft product shadow with 4px y-offset, 12px blur, 12-15% opacity, plus very faint UI-card shadow for realistic catalog layering.
- Graphic details: allow tasteful measurement ticks, tiny arrows, zoom brackets, barcode-like SKU block, page code, and Korean angle captions; these must support the product-detail purpose and not cover important product features.
- Layout density: make the sheet feel like a real premium online-store detail image, with enough information to look useful and editorial, while keeping the product visually dominant.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: Hasselblad X2D 100C with 120mm Macro at f/8 for detail fidelity; maintain accurate perspective and crisp surface rendering. If {카메라} provides a specific product-photo direction, follow it while retaining the Hasselblad macro commercial clarity.
- Lighting: studio side light from the left at about 45° with controlled fill from the right; preserve natural sheen on leather or synthetic surfaces and make stitching shadows legible. Adapt intensity to {라이팅} while keeping realistic highlights.
- Color grade: neutral commercial product grade with clean whites, true-to-source material color, slightly elevated contrast for edge definition, and believable surface texture in macro panels.
- Rendering quality: high-resolution e-commerce retouching, sharp material detail, realistic shadow falloff, clean mask edges, accurate logo/text reproduction from the source product, and square composition matching {비율}.

[6. MOOD]
Premium fashion e-commerce catalog — Net-a-Porter / SSENSE product-detail aesthetic with richer Korean retail annotation, refined studio realism, and editorial-grade product clarity.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: any rendered Korean labels must be short, clean, and legible. Suggested text: “대표컷”, “측면 라인”, “디테일 컷”, “소재 확대”, “컬러 확인”, “스트랩 구조”, “굽 높이”, “수납 라인”, “제품 디테일”, “2026 S/S”.
- Preserve the EXACT product from {원본 제품}: keep precise shape, proportion, texture, color, label, logo, branding, and any printed text unchanged.
- The layout must stay a multi-angle product presentation for {카테고리}; do not change the object into a different product, do not alter its construction, and do not beautify beyond realistic studio cleanup.
- Panel consistency: all views must clearly depict the same single product instance, with no mismatched parts or inconsistent materials across cuts.
- Added catalog graphics, labels, barcode-like marks, and callouts must be clearly secondary and must never obscure defining product details, logos, stitching, hardware, soles, handles, or material texture.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters
