- Background treatment: deep navy field with warm beige information panels, subtle charcoal overlays, gold staff-line graphics, small musical note accents, and elegant rectangular framing for a classic educational advertisement look.
- Use {학원명·로고}, {로고보조문구}, {모집시즌라벨}, {헤드라인}, {서브헤드라인}, {hero 이미지}, {악기 종류}, {대상·수업}, {강사진문구}, {체험수업일정}, {장소안내}, {신청방법}, {등록혜택}, {학원주소}, {전화번호}, {카카오아이디}, {QR문구}, {협력파트너}, {컬러 팔레트} placeholders exactly where variable content belongs.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Header area: Place {학원명·로고} at the top in a refined academy logo treatment, add {로고보조문구} below it, and place {모집시즌라벨} as a small badge or ribbon near the upper-right.
2. Headline area: Set {헤드라인} directly beneath the logo area in strong, readable Korean type, with {서브헤드라인} as a second line that explains the educational value.
3. Hero area: Show {hero 이미지} as the central visual anchor, cropped to emphasize a child-friendly music-learning moment; include realistic instrument textures, sheet music pages, teacher’s hand guidance if appropriate, and an academy classroom background.
4. Instrument strip: Present {악기 종류} as a row or grouped list with small instrument icons, thin gold rules, dot dividers, and a beige card background.
5. Class details block: Display {대상·수업} and {강사진문구} in concise information cards, using clear hierarchy similar to a Seoul academy enrollment poster.
6. Trial class block: Add event-style details with {체험수업일정}, {장소안내}, {신청방법}, and {등록혜택}; make this area feel actionable with a small “무료 체험 예약” CTA button shape.
7. Footer contact strip: Display {학원주소}, {전화번호}, {카카오아이디}, {QR문구}, and {협력파트너}; include a small QR-code placeholder square, map-pin icon, phone icon, chat icon, and sponsor/partner micro text.
8. Palette integration: Apply {컬러 팔레트} across background, accents, separators, badges, caption boxes, and text emphasis so the whole piece feels cohesive and premium.
9. Final polish: Keep edges crisp, spacing disciplined, and all Korean text fully legible while allowing realistic poster elements, musical graphics, and academy information details to enrich the design.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: Pretendard Bold for headline, Pretendard SemiBold or Noto Sans KR Medium for details, with a refined formal Korean academy feel; headline around 54–72px equivalent, subheadline around 30–38px equivalent, body around 24–32px equivalent, footer microcopy around 18–22px equivalent.
- Color palette: use {컬러 팔레트} as the governing palette; render as deep navy #0E1A2B, gold #C8A45D, warm beige #EADFCB, charcoal #2C2C2C, and ivory #F8F1E6 for small cards.
- Border/shadow: thin gold rules, subtle 10–15% opacity drop shadow under the hero image, layered beige panels, small circular badge shapes, staff-line ornaments, and clean rectangular framing without heavy glow.
- Poster realism: include print-ad details such as a small QR box, phone number line, address line, enrollment badge, class schedule label, and sponsor/partner area; Korean text should look typeset, aligned, and intentionally designed.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: Canon EOS R5 with RF 85mm f/1.2L portrait lens look, f/2.8–f/4, with brochure-style shallow depth where the hero remains crisp and the background stays orderly.
- Lighting: soft studio lighting from upper-left at 45°, gentle fill from front-right, controlled highlights on instruments, natural reflections on piano keys and violin varnish, no harsh glare.
- Color grade: deep navy and warm gold with muted beige highlights, slightly cinematic but restrained, similar to a premium education brochure or private academy ad.
- Material detail: show tactile paper-poster quality, satin print finish, subtle ink texture, realistic instrument surfaces, neat classroom ambience, and warm wooden accents in the hero image.

[6. MOOD]
Premium children’s academy brochure — a polished Seoul education ad aesthetic with trustworthy private lesson quality, warm encouragement, classical music refinement, and practical enrollment information that parents can act on immediately.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: 반드시 아래 문구가 정확히 보여야 함.

[1. PURPOSE]
Korean children’s art academy advertisement poster, vertical A4-style layout for print, apartment notice boards, parent community posts, and social promotion. Designed to communicate class offerings, trial-class event details, age range, academy identity, contact information, and the joyful process of children making art in a warm premium-education tone.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Top header area (about 15%): {학원명·로고} centered as a friendly brand lockup, with the {헤드라인} directly beneath it in a bold Korean headline style; add a small ribbon label reading {상단라벨} near the logo.
- Main hero area (about 42%): {hero 이미지} as the primary focal point, showing a bright child-art activity scene or a lively collage of children’s artworks, paint cups, brushes, paper textures, and classroom table details.
- Program information area (about 20%): {수업 종류}, {대상·일정}, and {수업특징} arranged in colorful rounded cards with small doodle icons such as crayons, stars, palettes, scissors, and clay shapes.
- Event and enrollment area (about 13%): highlight {체험수업} with date/time/venue style details, reservation note, and a visible QR-style box labeled {QR문구}.
- Footer area (about 10%): show {주소·연락처}, {하단문구}, and a small sponsor/partner strip reading {협력표기}; include page-ready poster details like phone number, KakaoTalk inquiry, and map-pin icon.
- Background treatment: soft educational poster look with pastel paper grain, layered construction-paper shapes, brush-stroke swashes, watercolor dots, tape corners, and child-friendly color blocks from {컬러 팔레트}.
- Spacing and framing: structured vertical poster flow with lively classroom details, readable hierarchy, playful sticker-like accents, and print-advertisement polish.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Brand zone: place {학원명·로고} at the top center with a friendly academy identity; include the small {상단라벨} badge as a seasonal enrollment cue.
2. Headline zone: set {헤드라인} as the main typographic anchor in a bold, highly legible Korean display style, sized larger than all other copy and supported by a short paint-brush underline.
3. Hero image zone: show {hero 이미지} in the central area with a warm classroom-advertising feel; include believable art materials such as watercolor pans, crayons, clay tools, paper scraps, a child’s drawing sheet, and small finished artwork thumbnails pinned like a mini gallery.
4. Class list zone: present {수업 종류} as a tidy but colorful list with icon bullets, small dividers, and pastel category chips so each class type is easy to read at a glance.
5. Schedule zone: show {대상·일정} in a compact information card with clear hierarchy, emphasizing age range, weekday time, weekend availability, and class format.
6. Feature zone: include {수업특징} as three small benefit badges, such as creative confidence, portfolio archive, and monthly mini exhibition.
7. Trial event zone: make {체험수업} visually prominent with event date, application deadline, venue, reservation method, and limited-seat wording; add {QR문구} beside a realistic QR placeholder square.
8. Footer zone: place {주소·연락처}, {하단문구}, and {협력표기} across the bottom with icons for phone, location, chat, and website; maintain strong legibility for print and mobile viewing.
9. Color support zone: use {컬러 팔레트} across accent bars, text highlights, rounded cards, brush strokes, stickers, and background panels so the poster feels cohesive and child-oriented.
10. Finishing zone: add subtle decorative elements such as rounded shapes, paper-cut edges, masking tape, pencil scribbles, small paint splashes, and hand-drawn stars while keeping the advertisement professional and parent-friendly.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: Pretendard ExtraBold for the headline, Pretendard SemiBold for support text, and Noto Sans KR Regular for details; headline around 72–96px equivalent, body around 28–40px equivalent, footer/contact around 22–28px equivalent.
- Color palette: {컬러 팔레트} with soft pastel pink, sunshine yellow, teal, and charcoal; use off-white background #F7F4EE or warm cream #F5EFE6 with colored paper panels and watercolor accents.
- Border/shadow: rounded panels with soft drop shadow 0px 8px 20px at 14% opacity; use thin charcoal separators, tape-corner details, sticker borders, and gentle highlight edges rather than harsh outlines.
- Poster details: add realistic print-ad elements such as small registration labels, benefit badges, event deadline, QR reservation box, map-pin icon, contact strip, and sponsor/partner line.
- Illustration/photo integration: combine the hero photo or collage with childlike doodle overlays, paper textures, brush strokes, and small artwork snapshots so the academy atmosphere feels lived-in and trustworthy.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: 50mm f/1.8 natural documentary look for the hero image, with a clean child-photo-ad aesthetic rather than cinematic distortion.
- Lighting: soft window light from upper-left at about 45°, with gentle fill from the front-right to keep skin tones, paper, paint, and artwork bright and readable.
- Color grade: pastel classroom grade with warm cream highlights, light pink accents, fresh yellow notes, teal details, and restrained charcoal text.
- Material realism: visible paper grain, crayon wax marks, watercolor bleed, matte sticker texture, soft shadows under craft objects, and realistic printed-poster ink density.

[6. MOOD]

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: must appear exactly as rendered in the default strings for {학원명·로고}, {상단라벨}, {헤드라인}, {수업 종류}, {대상·일정}, {수업특징}, {체험수업}, {QR문구}, {주소·연락처}, {하단문구}, and {협력표기}; all Korean characters must be clean and correctly formed.
- 필수 노출 문구: “○○ 키즈 아트”, “아이의 손끝에서 시작되는 세상”, “무료 체험수업”, “선착순 12명”, “상담 예약 QR”.

A realistic published workbook front cover with classroom-ready hierarchy, including issue/date information, unit label, sample exercise snippets, publisher mark, barcode-style retail block, and downloadable-material cue.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Main cover area: vertical B5 workbook cover layout with the headline occupying the upper 18–22%, the level/category band directly below, the central illustration and sample worksheet preview occupying the middle 45%, and the publisher/ISBN/barcode area placed in the lower 15%.
- Background treatment: warm hanji paper beige surface with subtle paper fiber texture, printed ink grain, and light tactile workbook paper feel; use small ruled-line, grid, or manuscript-paper motifs where appropriate for a Korean worksheet.
- Cover content density: include realistic educational details such as {권호·날짜}, {단원명}, {학습목표}, {예시문항}, {부가자료}, and {가격·ISBN} so the cover feels like an actual purchasable study sheet rather than a blank poster.
- Use {학습지 종류}, {레벨·대상}, {헤드라인}, {표지 일러스트}, {출판사·시리즈}, {컬러 팔레트} placeholders as the main design system.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Top header band: place {권호·날짜} as a small series/date line at the very top, then set {헤드라인} in a bold Korean serif headline, centered, with strong weight contrast between thick and thin strokes, occupying the upper 15–20% of the page.
- Subtitle/support line area: place {학습지 종류} and {레벨·대상} beneath the headline in smaller sans-serif text, formatted like a real workbook cover subtitle with a compact level badge and a clear subject tag.
- Unit and objective strip: add a horizontal learning strip reading {단원명} and {학습목표}, using small icons such as 연필, 체크박스, 말풍선, or 원고지 cells; keep it educational and print-ready.
- Central illustration zone: render {표지 일러스트} as a friendly educational illustration with crisp edges, flat-but-friendly styling, and clear separation from the background; combine it with a partial worksheet preview card showing {예시문항}, answer boxes, circled examples, and neat red correction marks.
- Lower publisher zone: position {출판사·시리즈} as a small publisher mark or series label near the bottom, with {부가자료} as a QR/download cue and {가격·ISBN} beside a barcode-style retail block.
- Overall structure: preserve a textbook cover composition with calm academic rhythm, clear reading order, realistic workbook microcopy, and balanced alignment suitable for a B5 printed Korean learning sheet.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use Pretendard or Noto Sans KR for body, labels, captions, badges, and exercise text, and a Korean serif such as Noto Serif KR or a bold 명조 style for the headline; headline weight 800–900, subtitle weight 400–600, microcopy weight 350–500, size contrast clearly visible.
- Color palette: use {컬러 팔레트} with dancheong red, hanji beige, charcoal, and restrained metallic gold accents; apply gold to small badges, rule lines, or unit markers only.
- Workbook realism: add thin ruled lines, manuscript-paper squares, check circles, small page tabs, chapter numbering, red teacher-style correction marks, and tiny caption labels to make the design feel like a real Korean study booklet.
- Border/shadow: use a soft printed-paper shadow, 2–4px y-offset, 10–14px blur, 12–18% opacity; if a frame appears, make it like a workbook trim line, subject divider, or printed rule rather than an ornate decoration.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: front-facing flat editorial layout, simulated as a clean graphic cover rather than a photographed scene; if any illustrative depth is used, keep it equivalent to a 50mm normal-lens perspective with no distortion.
- Lighting: even diffused studio light, no harsh directionality, with a very slight paper-highlight on the center area and soft falloff at the edges.
- Color grade: warm beige and dancheong red with charcoal text and restrained gold accents, similar to a Korean educational publisher cover with print-friendly saturation.

[6. MOOD]
Korean educational workbook cover — polished publisher-style textbook design with the calm clarity of a real school learning sheet, enriched by practical study cues, unit information, and familiar printed worksheet details.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: the rendered image must correctly show these verbatim Korean strings if included: “하루 한 장, 한국어 자신감”, “오늘의 맞춤법”, “받침을 바르게 써요”, “정답은 QR로 확인”.
- Keep all Korean characters crisp and fully legible; no broken syllables, no garbled spacing, no incorrect jamo composition.
- Maintain a real workbook cover hierarchy: date/series line, headline, level and category, unit objective, central illustration with sample worksheet preview, publisher and barcode area.
- The cover should include realistic Korean workbook microcopy such as slide/page number style labels, small captions, price/ISBN block, and downloadable-material cue without overpowering the main headline.

- Broken Korean characters
- Celebrity composites or altered real-person identity
- Text overflow outside the page frame

- Use a crisp white paper base with bright green and yellow accent panels, plus realistic textbook-cover details such as level badges, unit tabs, small sample-problem cards, curriculum tags, and a barcode/price area.
- Keep the layout readable and well-structured with authentic Korean workbook spacing, allowing useful cover information to sit around the main illustration without feeling empty.
- Place {학습지 종류}, {레벨·대상}, {헤드라인}, {표지 일러}, {출판사·시리즈}, {컬러 팔레트}, {비율} as editable content zones that remain balanced even when the text length changes.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Top header zone (upper 18%): set {학습지 종류} as a compact category label inside a rounded green tab, followed by {레벨·대상} in a smaller yellow sublabel; add small Korean curriculum text such as "초등 수학 집중 연습", "개념 → 유형 → 실전", and "VOL.05" near the header like a real series cover.

- Illustration zone (mid 45%): place {표지 일러} as a bright educational illustration cluster with numbers, geometric shapes, graph paper tiles, pencils, ruler, compass, eraser, small sticky-note labels, and a friendly mascot-like character solving a problem; include visible sample cards with Korean math phrases such as "오늘의 문제", "도형", "분수", "식 세우기", and simple equations like "12×3=36".
- Study-info strip (lower-mid 12%): add three small feature blocks with short Korean labels, for example "개념 체크", "유형 연습", "오답 노트", each with a tiny icon and page-like marker; add a subtle progress sticker reading "30일 완성" or "매일 2쪽".
- Publisher/series zone (lower 10%): place {출판사·시리즈} as a realistic logo-like publisher/series mark near the bottom, accompanied by a small address/contact line, edition/date label such as "2026 개정판", price text such as "정가 ₩7,500", and a barcode/ISBN-style rectangle at the lower right.
- Color system: apply {컬러 팔레트} across title bands, icon accents, divider rules, tabs, badges, sticker shapes, and small separators so the cover stays lively, disciplined, and print-ready.

- Color palette: use bright green, yellow, white, and charcoal from {컬러 팔레트}, with white as the dominant paper color, green and yellow as energetic learning accents, and charcoal for readable text contrast.

[1. PURPOSE]
English workbook cover for Korean educational publishing, vertical B5-style front cover, designed to read clearly as a real study guide on a bookstore shelf, classroom desk, or digital thumbnail.
Make it feel like a commercially printed Korean English-learning worksheet cover with a strong headline, clear level labeling, unit/course information, workbook badges, barcode area, and a friendly learning visual system depending on {학습지 종류} and {레벨·대상}.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Main title zone: place {헤드라인} across the upper 22% of the page, centered and dominant, with confident textbook-cover hierarchy and strong thumbnail readability.
- Subject label zone: show {학습지 종류} and {레벨·대상} as smaller supporting text near the title area, aligned like a real Korean workbook series label.
- Learning promise strip: include the exact Korean copy “매일 15분, 영어가 입에서 나온다” as a clear cover line beneath the title or in a colored ribbon.
- Illustration zone: center {표지 일러} as the main visual anchor occupying the middle 45–50% of the frame, surrounded by relevant study elements such as alphabet cards, notebook grids, pencils, speech bubbles, flashcards, check marks, and small English word samples.
- Publisher/series zone: place {출판사·시리즈} as a small imprint-style mark near the lower corner or top corner, legible like a real workbook publisher cue.
- Real cover details: add a top corner badge such as “STEP 01”, “VOL. 03”, or “개정판”, a small “QR 듣기 자료” label, unit preview tabs like “UNIT 01 인사하기 / UNIT 02 학교생활”, a lower back-cover-style barcode box, price text “정가 ₩12,000”, and tiny spine/credit text along one edge.
- Background treatment: educational cover surface with color blocking, ruled notebook lines, faint vocabulary patterning, soft paper grain, or subtle classroom icon texture using {컬러 팔레트}.
- Keep the composition portrait, stable, front-facing, and print-ready, with realistic trim/bleed awareness for a 1024x1536 B5 cover crop.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Background layer — Build a textbook-cover backdrop using the tones from {컬러 팔레트}; for children, use bright blue, yellow, and red blocks with crisp separation, playful notebook grid textures, letter patterns, and sticker-like labels; for adult versions, use off-white, charcoal, and one muted accent with refined study-note rules, section tabs, and clean editorial bands.
2. Hero title layer — Render {헤드라인} in the upper third with bold publication-style typography, sized to command attention while still allowing room for the course labels, badge, and learning promise strip.
3. Level and course information — Set {학습지 종류} and {레벨·대상} as compact informational labels beneath or beside the headline, using textbook hierarchy with realistic secondary copy such as “기초 회화 + 파닉스 + 문장쓰기”, “하루 2쪽 완성”, or “듣기·말하기 통합 워크북”.
4. Illustration layer — Place {표지 일러} in the center as a friendly cover visual; if child-oriented, make it cheerful with books, pencils, alphabet blocks, flashcards, speech bubbles reading “Hello!”, “I can do it!”, and cute classroom motifs; if adult-oriented, keep it polished with a notebook, coffee cup, pencil, vocabulary cards, calendar marks, and organized study graphics.
5. Workbook information layer — Add realistic printed details: “STEP 01”, “초급”, “워크북 + 음원 QR”, “UNIT 01 Greetings”, “UNIT 02 My School”, a small checklist “읽기 / 듣기 / 말하기 / 쓰기”, and a page-count/format line such as “128쪽 구성”. Keep these short and secondary to {헤드라인}.
6. Publisher mark layer — Add {출판사·시리즈} as a small branded series cue, tucked into a corner with discreet scale, like a real workbook imprint; include a tiny designer/editor credit line such as “기획 편집부 · 표지 일러스트 김하루” if it fits the layout.
7. Retail layer — Place a small barcode area at the lower right or lower left with “ISBN 979-11-0000-000-0”, “정가 ₩12,000”, and a tiny distribution note; make it look printed on the cover, not like a sticker floating above it.
8. Ratio handling — Preserve the vertical B5 cover feel of {비율}, optimized for a 1024x1536 portrait crop with clean trim edges, subtle paper thickness, and all essential text inside the printable cover area.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use Pretendard ExtraBold or Noto Sans KR Bold for {헤드라인}, 54–72px feel, with smaller Pretendard SemiBold or Noto Sans KR Medium for {학습지 종류}, {레벨·대상}, badges, unit tabs, and price details; if the tone is more classic, use a clean serif accent such as Nanum Myeongjo for one supporting line only.
- Color palette: follow {컬러 팔레트}; for child workbook style, use vivid #4A90E2 blue, #FFD84D yellow, and #FF5A4F red with fresh white panels and playful sticker accents; for adult style, use off-white #F7F5F0, charcoal #222222, and one muted accent such as sage #A7B8A1 or navy #1F3A5F.
- Print realism: include slight paper grain, realistic ink coverage, fine registration-like detail, subtle cover lamination sheen, and soft textbook-cover shadows such as 4px y-offset, 12px blur, and 15% opacity.
- Panels and labels: use thin clean outlines at 1–2px, colored tabs, round badges, ruled lines, speech-bubble frames, and small checklist icons that support the workbook theme.
- Layout discipline: use crisp print-like spacing, consistent alignment, and believable textbook hierarchy; decorative elements should reinforce English learning and classroom study, not compete with the headline.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: emulate a clean product-cover layout shot with a Canon EOS R5 and 50mm standard lens look, front-on orthographic presentation; if slight depth is needed, use a 35mm editorial cover framing while keeping the cover rectangular and paper-like.
- Lighting: use even studio softbox lighting from upper-left at about 45° with gentle fill from the right, producing soft cover shadows, readable ink detail, and a polished retail photography feel.
- Color grade: bright school-supplies palette for children or soft neutral editorial grade for adults, with controlled saturation, clean whites, crisp black text, and accurate color separation for print.
- Material detail: show realistic matte or semi-gloss workbook stock, subtle edge thickness, tiny barcode lines, fine type, and slightly tactile printed illustration texture.

[6. MOOD]
Korean educational publishing cover — like a polished EBS-style workbook or Oxford-style English study guide adapted for a Korean classroom, practical, friendly, content-rich, and ready for retail display.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: 반드시 다음 문구가 정확히 보여야 함: "매일 15분, 영어가 입에서 나온다".
- The cover must clearly communicate an English-learning worksheet/booklet with a textbook-like hierarchy, not a poster or magazine.
- Include realistic cover microcopy in Korean such as “기초 회화”, “듣기 QR”, “하루 2쪽”, “정가 ₩12,000”, and short unit labels, while keeping {헤드라인}, {학습지 종류}, {레벨·대상}, and {출판사·시리즈} visually accurate.
- All Korean labels must render without broken characters, spacing errors, or garbled punctuation.
- If {표지 일러} includes a character, keep the illustration clean, friendly, and anatomically correct; do not distort hands, faces, books, pencils, or stationery objects.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters
- Celebrity composites or unauthorized likeness

- Top header zone (about 18%): place {헤드라인} in large, bold Korean typography with a secondary English emphasis line if included in the headline; align center or slightly left depending on balance, with strong contrast against the background. Add small header metadata such as "VOL.247", "2026년 5월 시즌 광고", and "TRAVEL NOW" near the top edge.
- Hero zone (about 52%): render {hero 이미지} as the main visual centerpiece with cinematic commercial polish; for aircraft, show takeoff motion, runway perspective, airport windows, boarding lights, and distant travelers with luggage; for KTX/SRT/train, show departure or platform motion with platform markers, overhead signs, rails, and timetable boards; for bus, show premium long-distance travel atmosphere with terminal bays, road glow, and luggage loading details. Keep transport proportions realistic and perspective accurate.
- Promotional badge area (about 10%): place {할인·이벤트} in a compact, attention-grabbing box, angled ribbon, or ticket coupon panel, using gold or accent color fill with dark text. Add supporting short Korean microcopy such as "선착순 특가", "왕복 예약 혜택", "가족 동반 추천" without overpowering the main offer.
- Booking/info zone (about 12%): place {예매 정보} in structured lines or small blocks, with route, date, fare, and booking CTA styling. Include practical labels such as "예매 기간", "탑승 기간", "온라인 예매", "모바일 체크인", plus tiny transport icons, dotted ticket separators, and a QR-code-like square labeled "빠른 예매".
- Footer balance area (about 8%): use {교통수단} and {컬러 팔레트} to reinforce brand identity through decorative route lines, corner accents, sponsor-style blocks, small partner text like "공동 프로모션", contact line "고객센터 1588-0000", and a base band with barcode-style marks and fine print.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: bold modern Korean sans serif such as Pretendard or Noto Sans KR for the headline, weight 800–900, with 54–78px visual scale; use 400–500 weight for booking details and event copy, and allow select English words to sit in condensed uppercase for campaign energy.
- Color palette: use {컬러 팔레트} as the primary identity colors, supported by charcoal #1F1F1F, warm gold #C8A24A, off-white #F5F1E8, and one vivid accent color that matches the transport category.
- Border/shadow: soft drop shadow 0px 6px 16px at 18% opacity for the hero cutout or info cards; use thin divider lines in 1.5px gold or white to structure the poster.
- Layout detail: combine glossy ad photography with printed-poster realism, including ticket perforation lines, tiny terms text, route-map curves, platform/airport pictograms, small fare tags, and sponsor rectangles. All decorative elements should support a real transportation campaign look.
- Text density: include 2–3 short Korean promotional blurbs around the lower and side areas, for example "연휴 좌석 조기 오픈", "가족 여행 추천 노선", "주말 출발 추가 할인"; keep them readable and secondary to {헤드라인}.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: premium advertising photography look shot on a Phase One IQ4 with an 80mm lens for aircraft/travel subject clarity, or a 24–70mm full-frame commercial lens for broader transport scenes, f/4 to f/5.6 depending on depth.
- Lighting: controlled studio-style commercial lighting with soft key light from upper-left at about 45°, gentle fill from the front-right, and subtle rim light to separate the hero from the background; if the scene suggests departure time, add a faint dusk or early-morning atmosphere.
- Color grade: airline-and-rail campaign grade with crisp blues or reds depending on the brand palette, balanced by warm gold highlights, charcoal shadows, clean neutral whites, subtle terminal reflections, and realistic motion highlights.
- Material realism: glossy printed ad finish, semi-transparent information cards, metallic gold accents, reflective glass or platform surfaces, natural sky haze, and finely detailed transport textures such as windows, doors, wheels, rails, runway lights, or seat silhouettes.

[6. MOOD]
Premium Korean travel campaign — major airline and national rail holiday advertising aesthetic, like a polished airport lounge poster mixed with a high-end transport brand launch, filled with realistic seasonal travel anticipation, departure energy, and practical booking urgency.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: "고향 가는 길, 더 빠르게." must appear exactly if used in the headline.
- Korean text accuracy: {교통수단}, {할인·이벤트}, and {예매 정보} must be rendered in clean, legible Korean without broken characters.
- Include realistic Korean poster details such as "2026 시즌 특가", "예매 기간", "탑승 기간", "빠른 예매", "서울 ↔ 부산", or "김포 ↔ 제주" where appropriate, rendered cleanly.
- Composition invariant: the poster must keep a clear top headline, large hero center, promotional block, booking information block, sponsor/contact footer, and ticket-style details; do not collapse the hierarchy.
- If the hero includes people, they must look natural and anatomically correct, with believable travel clothing, luggage, gestures, and facial proportions.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters

[1. PURPOSE]
Vertical recruitment advertisement for working holiday, study abroad, and language school consultation. Designed as an A4-style poster for social media ads, agency lobby display, and Kakao/Instagram promotion, with a realistic travel-and-education sales layout that feels like a printed study-abroad campaign poster.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Top header: show {기관명} as a small agency label with {캠페인명} above the main headline, plus a tiny passport-stamp graphic and route-line decoration.
- Main headline: {헤드라인} set as the dominant Korean headline in the upper third, supported by {서브카피} as a compact subheadline.
- Middle hero zone: {hero 이미지} arranged as a premium travel brochure montage, including realistic details such as a boarding pass corner, suitcase handle, campus bulletin board, city skyline, airplane window reflection, and student study materials.
- Program highlight: {국가·프로그램} placed in destination cards or ribbon labels near the hero image, with flag-color accents, small map pins, airport-code style labels, and short program tags.
- Information modules: {서비스 안내}, {가격·패키지}, {상담혜택}, and {신청방법} placed in stacked cards beneath the hero, using icons, dividers, checklist marks, small captions, and readable price emphasis.
- Event and contact footer: {일정}, {장소}, {연락처}, {QR문구}, and {주최표기} displayed like a real consultation poster footer with a QR area, reservation badge, contact strip, and sponsor/partner-style label.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Header zone (top 15%): place {기관명}, {캠페인명}, and {헤드라인} in bold Korean typography, with a smaller English-style subtitle treatment if included, creating a polished education-ad style.
2. Hero zone (middle 42%): compose {hero 이미지} as the main visual anchor, using layered brochure-photo panels, passport stamp overlays, dotted flight route lines, a small luggage tag, and destination color chips to clearly communicate overseas travel, study, and departure readiness.
3. Destination label zone: display {국가·프로그램} in prominent pill, ribbon, or boxed labels near the hero area so the destination/program is instantly recognizable.
4. Service list zone: present {서비스 안내} as a concise checklist or icon-row module, each item separated by 1px dividers and short supporting captions for fast scanning.
5. Price and benefit zone: show {가격·패키지} in a strong price-callout block with contrasting emphasis, next to {상담혜택} as a badge or coupon-style panel.
6. Seminar/reservation zone: display {일정}, {장소}, and {신청방법} as event details with a ticket-like reservation strip, seat/limited-slot label, QR block, and phone/contact bar.
7. Footer zone: include {연락처}, {QR문구}, {주최표기}, small page-code text such as “AD-2026-SPRING”, and subtle printed-poster texture for realism.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use Pretendard Bold or Noto Sans KR Bold for the headline, Pretendard Medium for supporting text, and a modern sans-serif layout with size contrast roughly 54–72px for the title, 28–36px for section labels, and 20–28px for details.
- Color palette: follow {컬러 팔레트} with specific blocks of ochre/orange for Australia, maple red for Canada, soft pink for Japan, blue for the Philippines, anchored by charcoal #2B2B2B and off-white #F6F1E8.
- Graphic system: combine rounded info cards, boarding-pass perforation marks, passport stamp circles, dotted flight paths, small map-pin icons, checklist icons, QR placeholder, and coupon-style price tags.
- Border/shadow: use subtle 1px dividers, soft drop shadows with 4px y-offset, 12px blur, and 15% opacity for cards or modules; use slightly heavier shadow only for the price and reservation CTA.
- Layout rhythm: maintain a strong vertical flow from headline to hero to details, while adding realistic printed-ad elements such as micro labels, captions, footer codes, and contact information.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: editorial poster composite look, equivalent to a 35mm full-frame travel brochure shoot, with crisp depth separation and clean perspective; if a hero photo is implied, use a 24mm wide-angle travel composition or 85mm portrait framing depending on the source image.
- Lighting: bright commercial daylight with soft window-like diffusion from upper-left, slight fill from right, and balanced contrast to keep the text legible.
- Color grade: polished travel-ad grade using warm cream, saturated destination accents, and controlled charcoal shadows, with a contemporary Korean education-agency advertising finish.
- Texture and print feel: add subtle paper grain, brochure-like photo sheen, soft ink density variation, realistic card shadows, and tiny registration-style footer marks without reducing readability.

[6. MOOD]
Study-abroad agency campaign poster — polished Korean education-ad editorial with a premium travel brochure feel, energetic departure-day optimism, and practical consultation information that makes the ad look ready to print and publish.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: 반드시 아래 문구가 이미지에 정확히 들어가야 함: "GLOBAL STEP 유학센터", "2026 봄 출국 상담회", "내일을 영어로 시작하다.", "비자 신청", "어학원·홈스테이 매칭", "항공 예약", "출국 전 오리엔테이션", "필리핀 4주 패키지 199만원", "호주 워홀 컨설팅 99만원", "캐나다 학생비자".
- 추가로 포스터 안에 다음 상담 정보가 자연스럽게 보여야 함: "5월 18일(토) 14:00", "강남역 5번 출구 세미나룸", "무료 1:1 출국 플랜", "QR로 빠른 상담 예약", "02-1234-5678 · @globalstep_korea".
- The composition must remain a tall A4 vertical advertisement with clear hierarchy from headline to hero image to service, price, event details, and contact information.
- Keep all Korean typography crisp and fully legible, including small captions, price labels, phone number, QR caption, and destination labels.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters
- Celebrity composites or fake celebrity endorsements
- Misleading government-issued visa approval marks

[1. PURPOSE]
Korean travel budget settlement tracker card, account-book style infographic for trip planning and expense review.
Compact square template for sharing travel spending, budget comparison, exchange rates, daily totals, receipt notes, and money-saving tips in a realistic printed planner/card-news format.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Centered main tracker panel takes about 84% of the frame, built as a premium square card with rounded corners, subtle paper ledger texture, tab dividers, and a realistic printed account-book feel.
- Header zone occupies the top 14% with a bold title, trip date label, small page indicator, and tiny receipt-style metadata; the lower area is divided into structured budget blocks, a comparison chart, exchange-rate info, tip notes, and a mini settlement summary.
- Use {여행 일정·국가} as the main trip label, {카테고리} as the expense section labels, {예산 vs 실제} as the central comparison module, {환율 정보} as a compact side info box, {절약 팁} as small tip callouts, {컬러 팔레트} for the palette direction, and {비율} for the final canvas framing.
- Background should feel like a real desk-top planner spread: warm off-white ledger paper, faint grid lines, small receipt edges, a tiny paperclip, coin-like travel budget markers, and subtle sticker labels around the card while keeping the tracker information readable.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Header area (top 14%): place a strong Korean title in a clean accounting-dashboard style, with a short subtitle line underneath that frames the trip budget theme; add small printed details such as “TRIP MONEY LOG”, “정산일 2026.05.01”, “PAGE 01/05”, and “SAVE THIS”.
2. Trip summary strip: show {여행 일정·국가} as the primary trip context, aligned left in a neat label-value format, like a planner card header; include realistic micro labels such as “여행 기간”, “동행”, “결제 통화”, and “정산 기준”.
3. Category grid: arrange {카테고리} into 7 clearly separated rounded boxes, each with a small line icon placeholder, a tiny spent/remaining label, and a short receipt-code marker such as “R-01”, “R-02”, “R-03” for a real expense-log feel.
4. Budget comparison module: render {예산 vs 실제} as the visual focal point with paired horizontal bars, slim numeric badges, small up/down difference indicators, and tiny labels “예산”, “실제”, “절약”, “초과주의”.
5. Exchange-rate box: place {환율 정보} in a smaller right-side or lower-right callout with a thin border, compact text hierarchy, and a mini timestamp line like “환율 기준 09:00 업데이트”.
6. Savings tips box: stack {절약 팁} as three short checklist-style lines with quote marks preserved, using small tick icons, sticker-note styling, and tight line spacing; add a tiny CTA label “다음 여행 전 저장”.
7. Footer/accent region: use {컬러 팔레트} as a visual guide for the entire card, with printed separators, tiny color swatches, a page indicator “01 / 예산 정산”, a small QR-like decorative block, and a balanced infographic finish based on {비율}.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: Pretendard or Noto Sans KR for all labels; title in Bold 34–40px, section labels in SemiBold 18–22px, details in Regular 14–16px, with crisp accounting-sheet spacing and realistic printed microcopy.
- Color palette: ivory #F6F1E8, teal #2E8C8C, red accent #D94B45, charcoal #2F343A, plus warm gray #D8D2C8 for dividers and box fills.
- Border/shadow: 1.5px charcoal outline on key cards, soft drop shadow 0px 6px 18px rgba(47,52,58,0.10), very subtle inner highlight for a printed planner look.
- Add realistic editorial details: perforated receipt lines, small tab stickers, ledger row numbers, thin dividers, tiny icon labels, and restrained printed texture that makes the tracker feel physically designed rather than sterile.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: top-down flat lay look, Canon EOS R5 with 50mm lens at f/5.6, minimal perspective distortion, designed like a clean editorial infographic capture.
- Lighting: even studio softbox lighting from upper-left with a faint fill from lower-right, natural soft shadows under paper edges and small desk objects, paper texture visible but restrained.
- Color grade: warm ivory base with controlled teal and red accents, slightly desaturated charcoal text, crisp but not glossy.

[6. MOOD]
Practical editorial planner — like a premium personal finance spread from Monocle with the clean structure of a modern Notion template, enriched by real travel receipt details, saved-note stickers, and friendly Korean budget-tracking microcopy.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: the image must correctly include these exact Korean strings, with no broken characters: "여행 일정·국가", "항공·숙박·식비·교통·관광·쇼핑·기념품 — 7박스", "예산 200만원 vs 실제 187만원 / 항목별 막대 그래프", "USD 1,380원 / EUR 1,510원 / JPY 100엔 920원 — 작은 환율박스", "\"체크카드 환전 수수료 무료\" / \"공항버스 vs 택시 비교\" / \"현지 SIM 대신 eSIM\"".
- Also include realistic Korean tracker labels where space allows: "여행 예산 정산 트래커", "정산일 2026.05.01", "PAGE 01/05", "이번 여행 13만원 절약", "영수증 확인", "다음 여행 전 저장".
- All category boxes must remain clearly separated and readable, with consistent spacing and aligned edges across the grid.
- Keep the overall composition square and structured like a budget tracker card, not a travel poster or photo collage.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters
- Unauthorized celebrity likenesses

[INPUT]
- language: Korean
- output_size: 1024x1024
- format_note: {비율}

[1. PURPOSE]
Korean travel-prep informational card news graphic for passport, visa, and currency exchange. Designed as a shareable social carousel cover with an editorial public-information feel, combining practical checklist clarity with realistic travel-desk details.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Square carousel cover layout: a narrow top metadata strip, a strong headline band occupying about 18% of the frame, a central hero flat-lay occupying about 40%, and a lower information zone for step icons, caution box, page indicator, and CTA.
- Background uses matte white and cool-gray paper texture with deep navy framing, thin gold rules, subtle map-grid lines, airport code stamps, small route arrows, and checklist tick marks.
- Top metadata strip should read like a card-news issue label: “TRAVEL CHECKLIST | {발행일} | 카드뉴스 {슬라이드번호}”, with {발행처} as a small spine-style vertical credit along the left edge.
- Keep {헤드라인} large and centered at the top, with {보조카피} directly underneath as a smaller supporting line.
- Place {hero비주얼} in the middle as a realistic editorial travel-desk still life; include practical objects such as a passport-style booklet, visa application sheet, fictional entry stamp marks, USD/EUR/JPY cash, exchange receipt, itinerary memo, pen, boarding-pass-like paper, binder clip, and small travel pouch.
- Arrange {단계별안내} as a clear four-step pictogram flow, and place {주의사항박스} in a prominent caution callout near the lower third.
- Bottom navigation should include {페이지표시}, carousel dots, a save/share micro-icon pair, and {CTA문구} as a compact end-card CTA preview.
- Use {주제} as the guiding theme so the card immediately reads as passport, visa, and currency exchange preparation rather than generic finance or office stationery.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Top metadata zone: place “TRAVEL CHECKLIST”, {발행일}, and “카드뉴스 {슬라이드번호}” in small uppercase-style sans-serif with gold separators; add {발행처} vertically on the left spine margin like an editorial credit.
- Header zone: render {헤드라인} in bold Korean sans-serif, centered, with strong hierarchy; add {보조카피} below it in medium-weight Korean text and use thin gold separator rules above and below the title block.
- Hero zone: build {hero비주얼} as a crisp top-down flat lay. The passport-style booklet sits slightly left of center, currency notes and coins fan out to the right, a visa application sheet and boarding-pass-like paper overlap beneath, and a small exchange receipt shows Korean labels such as “환전 영수증”, “수수료”, and “우대율”.
- Practical micro-labels: add small sticky-note tags around the hero such as “여권 만료일 확인”, “비자 필요 여부”, “환율 알림”, and “사진 규격 체크” to make the graphic feel useful and lived-in.
- Step zone: render {단계별안내} as four numbered pictogram cards with icons for form, ID photo, payment, and pickup; connect the cards with small route arrows and keep label lengths balanced.
- Caution zone: set {주의사항박스} inside a charcoal callout box with white text, gold border, caution icon, and a small label reading “출국 전 필수 확인”.
- Bottom utility zone: include {환전팁} as a small one-line tip, then show “{페이지표시}” with five carousel dots, save/share micro-icons, and {CTA문구} in a navy pill-shaped button.
- Decorative information graphics may include dotted flight routes, passport-page line art, small currency symbols, and checklist boxes, all integrated into the editorial layout.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: Pretendard ExtraBold for the headline, Pretendard SemiBold for step labels, Noto Sans KR Medium for caution text, and Noto Sans KR Regular for metadata and microcopy; size hierarchy roughly 54–60 px / 26–30 px / 20–22 px / 14–16 px.
- Color palette follows {컬러팔레트}: deep navy #0B1F3A, gold #C8A24A, white #FFFFFF, charcoal #2B2F36, cool gray #E9EDF2, with a small travel-red accent #D64A3A for caution and stamp details.
- Border/shadow: thin 2px gold rules, soft shadow under hero objects with 4px y-offset, 14px blur, 12% opacity; layered paper pieces should cast subtle realistic contact shadows.
- Icon style: simple filled-line hybrid pictograms, rounded corners, consistent stroke weight, and small gold number circles.
- Text treatment: all Korean text should be horizontally aligned to a clear grid, with sufficient contrast against navy, white, and charcoal areas.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: top-down flat lay photographed like an editorial travel checklist, using a Canon EOS R5 with RF 35mm f/1.8 macro at f/5.6.
- Lighting: soft studio light from upper-left at 45° with a very light fill from the right, controlled reflections on glossy passport-style cover, gentle highlights on currency and paper texture.
- Color grade: deep blue, muted gold, crisp white, and charcoal with slightly cool highlights for a clean institutional print look.
- Material realism: matte paper grain, slightly embossed passport cover texture, crisp receipt thermal-paper feel, translucent sticky notes, and lightly worn travel-document edges.

[6. MOOD]
Premium public-information travel editorial — like a Condé Nast Traveler checklist page mixed with a clean government brochure layout, but warmer and more practical through real desk objects, micro-labels, and carousel UI details.

[7. CRITICAL]
- 반드시 다음 한글 문구가 정확히 보여야 함: 떠나기 전 7일, 이것만 챙기세요.
- 반드시 다음 주의사항 문구가 정확히 보여야 함: 여권 유효기간 6개월 이상 / 비자 면제 국가 vs 신청 국가 / 환전 수수료 비교
- 카드뉴스 표기: 카드뉴스 {슬라이드번호}, 페이지 표시 {페이지표시}, 발행일 {발행일}, 발행처 {발행처}가 읽히게 배치.
- CTA 문구 {CTA문구}와 환전 팁 {환전팁}을 하단에 작게 넣되 선명하게 렌더링.
- Step section must clearly show a four-step sequence with distinct numbered icons, route arrows, and balanced spacing.
- Keep all Korean text fully legible, with 깨짐 없는 한글 글자와 정확한 맞춤법.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters
- Celebrity composites or likeness swaps

[1. PURPOSE]
Korean hanok guesthouse / hanok stay advertisement poster, vertical A4-style editorial layout for social media and print use.
A premium travel poster that promotes traditional lodging, seasonal stay dates, cultural add-ons, local walking routes, and reservation information in one glance.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Poster uses a vertical travel-ad layout with the hero image occupying the upper 54–58% of the frame, a headline and seasonal event band crossing the upper-middle, and practical booking / guide / sponsor details stacked in the lower section.
- Main subject is {숙소·지역} represented through a serene hanok courtyard / eaves / maru / lattice-window scene, framed as the visual anchor.
- Background treatment should feel like warm hanji paper and aged wood textures, with ivory paper fibers, subtle brush-grain, dancheong accent graphics, and charcoal typographic dividers.
- Use {숙소·지역}, {헤드라인}, {hero 사진}, {숙박 정보}, {주변 안내}, {컬러 팔레트}, {행사명}, {일정}, {장소}, {예약 문의}, {가격 및 혜택}, {주최 협찬}, {지도 라벨}, {QR 문구} as editable content placeholders.
- Add realistic poster details: a small seasonal label, date/time/venue row, reservation CTA, tiny map-style guide strip, sponsor/partner line, and a QR-code placeholder box drawn as a printed graphic element.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Top hero area (mid 56%): {hero 사진} rendered as the main scenic block, showing hanok yard / maru / wooden eaves / lattice windows with warm lantern light, tea utensils, linen bedding glimpsed through the window, shallow depth of field, and a refined magazine-editorial crop.
- Seasonal event ribbon (top or over hero edge): {행사명} and {일정} placed like a printed travel campaign label, with a small monoline roof icon, moon motif, or dancheong corner ornament.
- Headline band (upper-middle 12%): {헤드라인} set prominently over a cream overlay or beneath the hero, using a dignified promotional hierarchy and a serif accent.
- Accommodation / price block (lower-middle 14%): {숙박 정보} and {가격 및 혜택} placed in a compact, highly legible information area with separator dots, check icons, and short lines.
- Local guide block (lower 10%): {주변 안내} and {지도 라벨} placed as a small walking-route strip with simple map pins, distance labels, and a charcoal route line.
- Booking / venue block (bottom 10%): {장소}, {예약 문의}, and {QR 문구} integrated with a small QR placeholder square, contact line, and call-to-action button shape.
- Sponsor footer (bottom edge): {주최 협찬} shown as a tasteful partner strip with small text and simple logo-like Korean wordmarks.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use Pretendard or Noto Sans KR for body text, with a high-contrast serif accent such as Nanum Myeongjo for the headline; headline weight 700–800, body weight 400–500, headline size larger by 2.2–2.8x than body.
- Color palette: ivory, hanji beige, dancheong red, and charcoal based on {컬러 팔레트}; use #F4EFE6 / #E7D8C4 / #9E2F2F / #2B2B2B as practical anchors.
- Graphic details: thin charcoal rules 1–2px, soft shadow only under the hero image (4px y-offset, 12px blur, 15% opacity), paper-grain overlays, small roof-line icons, brush-dot separators, map pins, and a printed QR placeholder.
- Poster information hierarchy should feel like a real boutique-stay advertisement: destination, emotional headline, stay package, date/time/venue, reservation method, nearby guide, sponsor/partner line.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: 35mm full-frame documentary interior/exterior hybrid look, with a 50mm f/1.8 feel for detail cuts; if featuring courtyard-wide framing, use a 24mm top-down/straight-on architectural perspective.
- Lighting: warm lantern practicals mixed with soft dusk ambient light, slightly from upper-left, with gentle fill from the front and a faint rim on wood edges.
- Color grade: warm ivory + muted wood brown + vermilion accents + deep charcoal, with low saturation and soft contrast resembling a premium travel magazine spread.

[6. MOOD]
Premium Korean travel editorial — a quiet Kinfolk x architecture digest feel, with the composed hospitality tone of a boutique hanok stay brochure, enriched by realistic printed-poster information and cozy evening travel details.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: the following strings must appear correctly and legibly in the design:
  - {숙소·지역}
  - {헤드라인}
  - {행사명}
  - {일정}
  - {장소}
  - {숙박 정보}
  - {가격 및 혜택}
  - {주변 안내}
  - {예약 문의}
  - {지도 라벨}
  - {QR 문구}
  - {주최 협찬}
- Fixed Korean labels may be added and must be readable: “체크인”, “체크아웃”, “예약하기”, “도보 여행”, “오늘의 다도”, “조식 포함”.
- Preserve the vertical A4 poster hierarchy: hero first, headline second, date/event cue third, booking and package info fourth, nearby guide and reservation CTA last.
- Keep all typography fully readable; no broken Korean characters, no garbled line breaks, no mixed-up order in the information blocks.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters
- Celebrity composites or unauthorized celebrity likenesses
- Distorted architecture, warped hanok structures, or inaccurate traditional details

[1. PURPOSE]
Vertical camping and glamping infographic guide poster for social sharing, campsite planning, and reservation promotion.
A practical A4-style editorial field guide that explains beginner camping, glamping package choices, car-camping basics, essential gear, easy campsite food, and on-site program information in one glance.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Overall layout: a richly detailed vertical infographic poster with a strong top-to-bottom reading flow; header occupies the top 14%, hero image the upper 27%, equipment cards the middle 26%, recipe cards the lower 21%, and a bottom information band for reservation, safety, sponsor, and contact details.
- Background treatment: off-white printed paper texture with subtle grain, faint topographic contour lines, tiny pine needles, tape-label accents, compass ticks, campfire spark marks, and soft earth-tone gradients that support the outdoor guide mood.
- Spacing and framing: layered editorial grid with consistent card spacing, rounded rectangle cards, thin dividers, small annotation stickers, and a structured hierarchy suitable for Korean text readability on mobile and print.
- Use {주제}, {헤드라인}, {hero 사진}, {장비 카드}, {요리 레시피}, {컬러 팔레트}, {가이드번호}, {발행일}, {장소}, {프로그램일정}, {입장정보}, {예약정보}, {문의연락처}, {안전팁}, {날씨라벨}, {스폰서문구}, and {푸터문구} as the customizable content anchors.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Header area (top 14%): place {가이드번호} and {발행일} as small editorial badges above or beside {헤드라인}; the headline should feel like a bold Korean outdoor masthead with a handwritten subtitle accent and tiny decorative stars, tent-line marks, and a small compass icon.
2. Hero area (upper 27%): show {hero 사진} as the main visual feature inside a wide rounded frame; overlay a warm campsite tint, a small caption tag for {장소}, and a weather sticker reading {날씨라벨} without covering the key tent, fire, or vehicle details.
3. Topic ribbon and intro line: place {주제} directly beneath the hero in a capsule banner; add small planning chips such as 1박 2일 기준, 초보 추천, 가족·커플·차박 OK to make the guide feel useful and realistic.
4. Equipment section (middle 26%): convert {장비 카드} into an exactly 8-item icon-and-label grid under the visible section title 필수 장비 8종; each item should have a simple camping pictogram, a short Korean label, and tiny practical notes such as 방수, 보온, 충전, 접이식, or 2인 기준.
5. Recipe section (lower 21%): present {요리 레시피} as an exactly 5-item mini-card set under the visible section title 캠핑 요리 5종; each card may include small food icons, tiny food-detail shots, prep time badges, heat-level dots, or one-line serving tips.
6. Program and reservation strip: add a compact poster-style information row with {프로그램일정}, {입장정보}, {예약정보}, and {문의연락처}; include a QR-code style square labeled 예약 QR, a ticket-stub graphic, and a small map-pin marker for the location.
7. Safety, palette, and sponsor footer: show {안전팁} as a field note on a kraft-paper sticker; show {컬러 팔레트} as a narrow swatch row with labeled color chips; finish with {스폰서문구} and {푸터문구} in a small sponsor/contact area.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use Pretendard ExtraBold or Noto Sans KR Bold for the main headline, Pretendard Medium for labels, and a handwritten Korean brush style only for the subtitle accent; title size should dominate the page while body labels stay compact and crisp.
- Color palette: use {컬러 팔레트} with deep forest green, warm beige, amber, and charcoal as the primary tones; accent lines can use muted olive, soft cream, campfire orange, and faded map-blue for functional tags.
- Border/shadow: apply thin charcoal rules, rounded card corners, kraft-paper labels, washi-tape tabs, map-pin callouts, small illustrated stickers, and soft drop shadows with 4px y-offset, 12px blur, and about 15% opacity for a tactile printed infographic feel.
- Icon system: camping gear icons should be consistent in stroke width; recipe icons can be slightly warmer and more illustrated, with tiny steam lines, grill marks, mugs, marshmallows, and skillet silhouettes.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: editorial lifestyle photo look, shot like a 35mm documentary frame for the hero and a 50mm product-detail feel for the small cards; straight perspective, natural depth, and no extreme distortion.
- Lighting: warm natural daylight with soft diffused sunlight from upper-left, gentle fill from the right, and a slight amber bounce to echo campsite firelight.
- Color grade: earthy deep green + beige + amber + charcoal, with subdued contrast, lightly desaturated shadows, warm highlights, and a calm outdoor field-guide aesthetic.

[6. MOOD]
Premium outdoor editorial infographic — like a Korean campsite field guide, a warm travel magazine spread, and a practical reservation poster combined.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: the following default Korean strings must appear correctly and legibly in the rendered image: 오늘 밤, 별빛 아래 잠들기.; 캠핑 입문 또는 글램핑 패키지 또는 차박 가이드; 필수 장비 8종; 캠핑 요리 5종; 캠프 가이드 VOL.03; 2026년 5월 18일 발행.
- Realistic guide details must be visible and readable: 북한강 숲속 캠핑장 · 경기 가평; 5월 30일 토요일 15:00–21:00; 입장 ₩7,500 · 사전 예약 권장; 예약 QR · @campfield.kr; 문의 010-2486-1536.
- Safety and footer text must be included as small but readable Korean print: 불멍은 지정 화로대에서만 · 쓰레기는 되가져가기; 스폰서 | 로컬 아웃도어 마켓; 초보 캠퍼를 위한 1박 2일 체크리스트.
- Layout invariants: the image must remain a vertical A4-style infographic with a clear top-to-bottom reading order, exactly 8 equipment items, exactly 5 recipe items, and consistent Korean text rendering.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications / government approval marks
- Broken Korean characters or unreadable Hangul
- Celebrity composites or recognizable public figures used as campers

[INPUT]
- language: Korean
- output_size: 1024x1536

[1. PURPOSE]
Korean travel guidebook cover for a specific city/country, vertical B6-style book jacket for bookstore shelves and online thumbnail use.
Realistic editorial cover that combines a city landmark illustration/photo with bold Korean headline typography, publisher branding, edition information, short travel feature blurbs, and practical guidebook retail details.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Single-book cover composition in a strict vertical frame: the main landmark artwork occupies about 55% of the upper-middle area, the headline copy sits in the lower third, and the series title anchors the top area like a real bookstore travel guide.
- Background is a tactile print-style field with subtle paper grain, faint ink texture, and layered city-map or transit-line motifs using the palette from {컬러 팔레트}; the cover should feel like a finished printed book jacket, not a blank mockup.
- Maintain strong editorial hierarchy on all sides, with the publisher mark, barcode/ISBN area, price label, small edition note, and travel-guide metadata placed naturally around the bottom and side zones.
- Add 2–3 short Korean feature blurbs that fit the destination, such as “현지인이 추천한 동네 산책”, “3박 4일 핵심 코스”, “카페·미술관·야경 루트”, set smaller than the main headline.
- Include realistic book-cover microcopy: “2026 최신개정판”, “MAP INSIDE”, “VOL.247”, “₩18,800”, “ISBN 979-11-0000-247-0”, and a small barcode box near the lower-left or lower-right.
- Use {도시·국가}, {가이드북 시리즈}, {표지 일러}, {헤드라인 카피}, {출판사·시리즈}, {컬러 팔레트}, {비율} as customizable placeholders.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Top area (about 12%): set {가이드북 시리즈} in small series-title type, centered or slightly upper-left depending on the cover layout, with generous tracking and a compact editorial feel. Add a small edition/date label nearby, for example “2026 최신개정판” or “VOL.247 · MAY 2026”.
2. Main visual area (mid 55%): place {표지 일러} as the hero artwork, framed with crisp edges and a polished travel-poster treatment; if the artwork is photographic, keep it cover-ready with a believable cutout or printed-photo panel, and if illustrative, preserve flat graphic clarity while adding small contextual city details such as street signs, skyline silhouettes, café awnings, transit lines, river shapes, foliage, or neighborhood textures that match {도시·국가}.
3. City label layer: integrate {도시·국가} as a prominent destination cue near the hero art, either as a subtitle, ribbon, capsule label, or large typographic layer behind/around the landmark. Add a small Korean descriptor such as “도시별 해외여행 가이드” or “걷고 먹고 머무는 여행법”.
4. Feature blurb layer: place 2–3 short Korean blurbs around the main visual or between the visual and headline, using compact editorial typography. Example blurbs: “현지 맛집 48곳”, “반나절 근교 코스”, “초보 여행자 체크리스트”. Keep them clearly secondary to {헤드라인 카피}.
5. Headline block (lower 18%): set {헤드라인 카피} in bold Korean display type, large enough to dominate the lower third, with strong contrast against the background and tight line breaks for a commercial cover look.
6. Bottom strip (about 8%): place {출판사·시리즈} as a small publisher mark in the lower-right corner. Add a practical retail block with barcode/ISBN, price “₩18,800”, and a tiny credit line such as “사진·일러스트 편집부” or “TRAVEL EDIT TEAM”.
7. Side/spine cue: include a very thin visible book-spine edge or vertical side text if the composition allows, with small text such as “{가이드북 시리즈} · {도시·국가}” to make the cover feel like a real printed guidebook.
8. Overall layout: keep the cover visually stable and instantly readable at thumbnail size, while adding authentic guidebook details, destination texture, map fragments, route markers, and printed production marks that support the travel concept.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use Pretendard ExtraBold or Noto Sans KR Black for {헤드라인 카피}, 42–64px visual scale; use Pretendard Medium or Noto Sans KR Regular for {가이드북 시리즈}, {출판사·시리즈}, edition labels, feature blurbs, ISBN, and price, 12–24px scale; add subtle tracking to the series title for a professional book-cover look.
- Color palette: follow {컬러 팔레트} precisely, typically combining city-specific accent tones with white and charcoal; examples include Tokyo pink, Paris blue, Bali green, clean white, and deep charcoal. Use accent colors for labels, route lines, map pins, and small typographic dividers.
- Print finish: create a realistic matte-coated book-cover finish with visible paper grain, faint ink registration texture, subtle edge shadow, and a soft drop shadow under the hero artwork if needed, about 4px y-offset, 12px blur, 15% opacity; avoid heavy bevels or glossy plastic effects.
- Layout details: include a small barcode area, edition/date label, price, ISBN-style number, destination category tag, and short travel blurbs. These details should look printed on the cover, aligned to a professional editorial grid.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: if using photography for {표지 일러}, emulate a full-frame 85mm f/1.8 or 50mm f/1.4 travel/editorial shot, crisp and cover-ready; for illustration, keep perspective clean like a travel poster with controlled depth.
- Lighting: soft daylight from upper-left at roughly 45°, with mild fill from the front and no harsh specular highlights; if the scene suggests a real city view, use overcast diffused light or late-afternoon golden-hour warmth depending on the city palette.
- Color grade: print-friendly editorial grading with clean whites, controlled contrast, and city-specific accent color emphasis; keep saturation moderate and avoid neon overshoot.
- Material realism: show slight paper tooth, printed ink density, tiny alignment marks or microtext where appropriate, and a believable book-cover surface so the result reads as an actual published travel guide.

[6. MOOD]
Premium bookstore travel-guide editorial — the polished, practical feel of a Lonely Planet / National Geographic Traveler cover with clean Korean typography, destination-first clarity, and the lived-in richness of a guidebook packed with routes, places, maps, and travel tips.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: 반드시 아래 문자열이 정확히 보여야 함:
  - {도시·국가}
  - {가이드북 시리즈}
  - {헤드라인 카피}
  - {출판사·시리즈}
- Additional Korean cover text may include: “2026 최신개정판”, “도시별 해외여행 가이드”, “현지인이 추천한 동네 산책”, “3박 4일 핵심 코스”, “카페·미술관·야경 루트”, “MAP INSIDE”, “₩18,800”.
- All Korean characters must render cleanly with no broken glyphs, no spacing corruption, and no incorrect line breaks inside the key headline.
- Keep the city landmark and headline hierarchy consistent with a real guidebook cover: main artwork dominant, headline bold, feature blurbs secondary, publisher mark small, barcode/ISBN and price readable but not distracting.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]

- Maintain a strong center axis and readable separation between hero, headline, schedule, viewing info, sponsor area, and footer accents.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Top header strip: place {팀·대회} as a compact category label near the top center with thin divider lines, plus small supporting text such as MATCH DAY, VOL.247, 2026년 시즌, and 응원 카드.
2. Main headline zone: set {헤드라인} in the upper third using oversized bold type, slightly condensed esports poster style, strong contrast against the dark background, and a subtle glow or outline that matches {컬러 팔레트}.
3. Hero centerpiece: render {hero 이미지} as the focal visual in the mid-frame, with crisp cutout edges, realistic fabric/armor/jersey texture if applicable, subtle glow, light flares, layered depth, and broadcast key art energy.
4. Fan energy layer: behind and around the hero, add stadium LED strips, blurred crowd lights, floating shards, team-color ribbons, cheering light sticks, or graphic speed lines that support {팀·대회} without covering key text.
5. Match info block: place {일정·매치} in a structured lower-third panel, using clear line breaks and icon-like separators for date, time, opponent, match type, and venue; include fixed Korean labels such as 일정, 경기, 상대, 장소.
6. Viewing info block: position {티켓·시청} beneath the schedule as a secondary but prominent utility section, visually grouped with the match info for fast scanning; include label text 예매 / 생중계, 시청, 알림 설정.
7. Ticket and CTA details: add a small QR-style placeholder box labeled 모바일 티켓, a short CTA chip reading 함께 응원하기, and a tiny channel handle such as @lck_fan_card or @worlds_watch.
8. Sponsor/footer band: place a slim accent band using {컬러 팔레트}, with small sponsor placeholders such as PARTNER, FAN ZONE, LIVE VIEWING, page-style code NO.05, and esports-style separators to make the card feel production-ready.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use Pretendard ExtraBold for the headline, Pretendard SemiBold for labels, and Noto Sans KR Medium for details; headline size should feel poster-scale, with compact tracking and strong vertical emphasis.
- Color palette: use {컬러 팔레트} plus deep navy #0B1020, charcoal #161A22, off-white #F3F5F7, and metallic highlight tones for accents.
- Border/shadow: apply crisp panel edges with soft drop shadows, 4px y-offset, 14px blur, 18% opacity; add thin neon-like edge glows around the hero, headline, match panels, QR box, and CTA chips.
- Graphic system: use angled panels, scoreboard tabs, tiny rule lines, diagonal slashes, translucent glassmorphism info boxes, LED-dot texture, and small numeric codes to create a realistic esports broadcast design.
- Text density should feel like a real social match poster: include 2–3 short Korean support blurbs such as 승리를 향해, 오늘의 관전 포인트, 팬 응원 모집, while keeping the main hierarchy immediately readable.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: simulated Canon EOS R5 broadcast key art look, 85mm f/1.4 portrait feel for the hero depth, with a polished studio composite aesthetic and realistic material detail.
- Lighting: dramatic arena lighting with a strong key from upper-left, cool rim light from upper-right, low backlight haze, LED reflections, and color streaks that suggest stage energy and competition intensity.
- Color grade: deep navy, charcoal, team accent red/yellow/gold, with controlled contrast, slightly boosted highlights, crisp blacks, and glossy broadcast-poster finishing.
- Finish: high-resolution vertical social poster with tactile printed-promo details, subtle grain, sharp typography, clean panel alignment, and premium esports event-card realism.

[6. MOOD]
High-stakes championship promo — Riot Games Worlds key art meets premium Korean esports broadcast poster, amplified with fan-zone energy, match-day urgency, and collectible cheering-card details.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: the following verbatim Korean strings must appear correctly if included in the final design: 롤드컵, LCK, 일정, 시청.
- Additional Korean text rendered in the image should be short and clean, for example: 승리를 향해, 예매 / 생중계, 함께 응원하기, 오늘의 관전 포인트, 모바일 티켓.
- Keep all text clean, sharp, and fully legible with no broken Korean characters.
- Preserve a strong esports poster hierarchy: hero, headline, schedule, viewing info, CTA, and sponsor/footer details must remain clearly separated and aligned.
- Do not change or omit the placeholders {팀·대회}, {헤드라인}, {hero 이미지}, {일정·매치}, {티켓·시청}, {컬러 팔레트}, {비율}; integrate them naturally into the final card.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]

- Broken Korean characters

[1. PURPOSE]
Korean ski/snowboard season pass advertisement poster, vertical A4-style promotional layout for winter resort marketing.
Designed for social-media and print-friendly campaign use with a bold headline, immersive night-slope hero scene, season pass pricing, benefit highlights, event details, sponsor area, and a direct ticket-purchase CTA.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Main subject: a dramatic ski/snowboard slope hero scene occupying the upper 55% of the frame, with {hero 이미지} as the visual anchor, featuring a rider carving through powder, visible snow spray, distant chairlifts, slope floodlights, safety netting, pine silhouettes, and a warm lodge glow in the background.
- Header zone: top 16% features {헤드라인} as the primary attention point in a compact promotional masthead, supported by a small season label such as SEASON PASS 2026 and OPENING SPECIAL.
- Resort/brand callout: {스키장} placed near the header or upper-mid area as a supporting identifier, paired with a realistic resort badge-style wordmark treatment, mountain icon, and small location/date label.
- Pricing/info block: {시즌권 정보} placed in a strong mid-lower information panel with clear hierarchy, layered price cards, red urgency tag, and ticket-purchase cue.
- Benefits block: {포함 혜택} arranged in a concise lower section, using short stacked lines, icon-like pictograms, dividers, and small explanatory sublabels for quick readability.
- Poster event details: include date/time/venue lines such as 2026.12.01 시즌 오픈, 운영시간 08:30–22:00, 장소: 메인 슬로프·스노우파크, plus ticket info 예매: 공식 홈페이지 / 현장 매표소.
- Sponsor/footer area: add a realistic sponsor strip near the bottom with small text such as 공식 파트너, 스키스쿨, 렌탈샵, 리조트 호텔, 푸드코트, plus a tiny barcode/QR-style ticket block and contact line.
- Background treatment: cold winter atmosphere with icy blue-to-navy gradient field, layered snow texture, drifting snow particles, illuminated piste map lines, lift cable silhouettes, and high-contrast night-slope lighting effects.
- Framing direction: clean vertical ad composition with strong commercial hierarchy, energetic layered panels, visible campaign details, and realistic resort-advertising density suited to {비율}.
- Use {스키장}, {헤드라인}, {시즌권 정보}, {hero 이미지}, {포함 혜택}, {컬러 팔레트}, {비율} placeholders exactly as written.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1) Top header strip: place {스키장} as a small but clear resort label above or beside the main headline, aligned to the upper area with strong contrast against the dark winter background. Add compact supporting text: WINTER RESORT, 2026–27 SEASON, and 개장 D-30.
2) Main headline zone: render {헤드라인} in oversized bold Korean typography, with the most important phrase emphasized in white and red accents, centered across the upper third for immediate visibility. Add a short Korean cover-line style blurb: 올해 가장 빠른 시즌 준비.
3) Hero image field: build {hero 이미지} across the central upper-to-mid area, showing a dynamic slope scene with rider silhouettes, snow spray, groomed snow tracks, chairlift towers, floodlights, mountain ridgeline, and night resort atmosphere that feels energetic and premium.
4) Season pass info panel: set {시즌권 정보} inside layered cards in the mid-lower section, using clear numeric hierarchy and spacing so pricing reads at a glance. Include red urgency tags such as 얼리버드 한정, 선착순 마감, 온라인 예매 가능.
5) Benefits panel: present {포함 혜택} as a compact list in the lower third, with separators, small ski/lift/rental/hotel/food pictograms, and short sublabels so each benefit feels like a real resort promotion.
6) Event and ticket strip: below the benefits, include date/time/venue and purchase information: 시즌 오픈 2026.12.01, 운영시간 08:30–22:00, 장소 메인 슬로프·스노우파크, 예매 공식 홈페이지 / 현장 매표소.
7) Footer information area: include sponsor logos as generic text labels, small barcode/QR-style graphic, contact 1588-2627, website winterpass.co.kr, and fine-print style notes such as 기상 상황에 따라 운영 일정 변동 가능.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: Pretendard ExtraBold for the headline at very large size, Pretendard SemiBold for labels, Noto Sans KR Medium for information blocks; keep the headline tight and the info text highly legible.
- Color palette: use {컬러 팔레트} exactly as the campaign base, with ice blue, white, navy, and red accent tones; keep whites crisp and blues cold rather than cyan-neon.
- Border/shadow: use subtle panel edges and a soft drop shadow with 4px y-offset, 12px blur, 15% opacity; use stronger red outline only for urgent price tags and CTA buttons.
- Layout accents: thin separator lines, compact info cards, small red highlight tags, slope-map contour lines, snowflake micro-patterns, ticket-stub notches, and diagonal speed streaks to reinforce urgency and winter sports energy.
- Poster realism: make the ad feel like a finished seasonal resort campaign with production details, sponsor strip, barcode area, operating schedule, and a polished print-ready hierarchy.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: wide 24mm flat promotional perspective with a clean advertising look, combined with a high-resolution sports-action feel similar to a Canon EOS R5 + 24-70mm f/2.8 at 35mm, f/4.
- Lighting: night-slope lighting with strong practical resort lights from the upper-right and upper-left, plus cool ambient fill from the snowy ground; crisp highlights on snow spray, reflective goggles, jacket edges, lift cables, and illuminated signage.
- Color grade: icy blue, cool white, deep navy, and selective red accents; high contrast but controlled, with clean winter advertising saturation.
- Material detail: visible packed snow texture, powder crystals, frosted typography shadows, glossy laminated ticket-card panels, subtle paper grain, and realistic poster-print finish.

[6. MOOD]
Premium winter sports campaign poster — a high-energy resort advertisement with the crisp, commercial clarity of a professional ski brand launch, packed with believable season-pass details, event excitement, and a night-resort atmosphere.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: the following Korean strings must appear correctly and clearly in the rendered image: 눈 위의 자유, 시즌 시작!, 2026~27 시즌권, 얼리버드 99만원, 일반 159만원, 학생할인 25%, 리프트 무제한, 장비 대여 30%, 리조트 숙박 30%, 식음료 10%.
- Additional poster text should appear clearly where appropriate: 시즌 오픈 2026.12.01, 운영시간 08:30–22:00, 장소: 메인 슬로프·스노우파크, 예매: 공식 홈페이지 / 현장 매표소, 문의 1588-2627, 선착순 마감, 공식 파트너.
- The overall composition must preserve a bold vertical advertisement hierarchy with clear headline, price block, benefits block, event details, ticket CTA, and sponsor/footer information.
- Hero scene must remain winter-sport themed with ski/snowboard slope energy, snow splash, resort lights, mountain background, and realistic night-slope atmosphere.
- Keep all typography clean and fully legible; Korean characters must not break or deform.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters
